item.title: Lindt got chocolate price hikes wrong, chairman says after CEO's ouster
item.description: Lindt & Sprüngli has struggled because it misjudged how consumers would respond to price increases, the chair of the Swiss chocolate maker said, days after the company ousted its CEO over concerns about its performance.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lindt & Sprüngli (LISN.S) has struggled because it misjudged how consumers would respond to price increases, the chair of the Swiss chocolate maker said, days after the company [USN:L6N4650EX TEXT:"ousted"] its CEO over concerns about its performance. In an interview with the NZZ am Sonntag newspaper, Executive Chairman Ernst Tanner said the firm, whose shares have tumbled more than 25% this year after recent outlook [USN:L8N45L05W TEXT:"cuts"], was largely suffering because it had misread the market in Germany. "We misjudged how customers would respond to price increases. After cocoa prices reached historic highs from 2024 onwards, we wanted to pass on those additional costs. In doing so, we overestimated how much we could raise prices without hurting demand," he said. "For some consumers, our products clearly became too expensive in recent months." "Lindt & Sprüngli as a whole, however, is not in crisis," Tanner added, arguing the company's shares are now undervalued. "In the Americas and the Far East, we'll achieve our growth targets of 6% to 8% this year as well." Tanner, 80, who was CEO from 1993 to 2016 and has been chairman for over three decades, rejected the suggestion that he should stand down, saying he had important work to do to get Lindt back on track. "Once that's been achieved, I look forward to turning to the next phase of my life," he said. Tanner said the company had already cut some prices as it seeks to lift sales volumes, and would have more scope to do so once cocoa prices returned to more normal levels. He said there would not be group-wide job cuts and that the firm wanted to keep growing. Still, he said thrift was required and that bonuses would be affected in the Germany-Switzerland-Austria region as targets had been missed.

item.title: Bolsonaro y Lula reúnen a multitudes de seguidores antes de balotaje presidencial en Brasil
item.description: El senador Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva cerraron el sábado sus campañas para la segunda vuelta de las elecciones, movilizando a multitudes de seguidores en un último esfuerzo por ganarse a los votantes indecisos en una contienda que aparece totalmente abierta.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Cardoso
item.content:encoded: El senador Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva cerraron el sábado sus campañas para la segunda vuelta de las elecciones, movilizando a multitudes de seguidores en un último esfuerzo por ganarse a los votantes indecisos en una contienda que aparece totalmente abierta. Ambos candidatos aparecen prácticamente empatados en las encuestas de cara al balotaje del domingo tras un resultado mejor de lo esperado de Bolsonaro en la primera vuelta. Lula, que busca su cuarto mandato, comenzó su último día de campaña con una marcha por la playa de Copacabana, donde miles de simpatizantes se unieron al actual presidente bajo un sol abrasador. "Vamos a ganar las elecciones por una sencilla razón: es cierto que el pueblo quiere un cambio, y el pueblo quiere un cambio para mejor, el pueblo quiere avanzar. El pueblo no quiere dar marcha atrás", declaró Lula a periodistas antes del mitin. Más tarde, el presidente encabezó otra marcha en São Paulo, pasando por la Avenida Paulista, donde una multitud se reunió para mostrarle su apoyo. "Estoy emocionada. He venido en metro y ha sido muy emocionante ver a todo el mundo. Una energía que queremos para Brasil. Brasil es nuestro", dijo Gisele Passos, una empresaria de 61 años. Para muchos seguidores de Lula, los mítines tuvieron un tono agridulce. El presidente, de 80 años, se encuentra en su último intento por ser elegido, lo que dotó a los últimos actos de la campaña de un aire de despedida. "Es único. Tiene una trayectoria realmente maravillosa, increíble y llena de lucha. Estamos muy orgullosos de ello", afirmó Olga Leal, una jubilada de 62 años. Bolsonaro, por su parte, se unió a una caravana de motos en Belo Horizonte, con la mirada puesta en los votantes del crucial estado de Minas Gerais. Ningún candidato ha ganado la presidencia sin imponerse allí desde el retorno de la democracia al país en la década de 1980. "El momento está a punto de llegar. Quedan pocas horas para que cambiemos el destino de nuestra nación durante los próximos 30 o 40 años", afirmó el hijo mayor del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro en un video publicado en las redes sociales. Posteriormente participó en una marcha en Barra da Tijuca, en Río de Janeiro, frente al complejo residencial donde vivía su padre. Jair Bolsonaro se encuentra bajo arresto domiciliario en Brasilia tras haber sido condenado a más de 27 años de prisión por intento de golpe de Estado tras perder las elecciones de 2022 frente a Lula.

item.title: UK budget set to hand English mayors new borrowing powers, growth funding
item.description: British finance minister John Healey will use next week's budget to hand mayors in England new funding and powers, including a £1.5 billion ($2 billion) borrowing facility, as part of plans to move economic decision-making out of Westminster.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey will use next week's budget to hand mayors in England new funding and powers, including a £1.5 billion ($2 billion) borrowing facility, as part of plans to move economic decision-making out of Westminster. The measures include £285 million of seed funding next year under a new "Good Growth" scheme, which the finance ministry said would let local leaders invest in their own growth priorities without seeking permission from central government. "I'm calling time on local leaders going cap in hand to Westminster. That is no way to run a country," said Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Here are the key points: • The Good Growth funding is designed to reduce local leaders' reliance on fragmented bidding pots from central government • The funds can be used for housing, regenerating high streets and improving transport links • The government will work with mayors to design the £1.5 billion borrowing facility, which it said would give them access to capital to back local growth projects • Strategic authorities will receive a further £150 million next year to build up staff and expertise as they take on bigger budgets ($1 = 0.7478 pounds)

item.title: Trump set to announce plan by Audi to build US factory in Georgia, source says
item.description: US President Donald Trump is expected to announce on Saturday that Volkswagen's premium subsidiary Audi plans to build a new assembly plant in Georgia that will produce 200,000 SUVs annually, a government official told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump is expected to announce on Saturday that Volkswagen's (VOWG.DE) premium subsidiary Audi plans to build a new assembly plant in Georgia that will produce 200,000 SUVs annually, a government official told Reuters. Trump, who has urged automakers to build more vehicles in the United States and imposed significant tariffs on foreign-made cars and trucks, plans to make the announcement in Georgia near where Audi intends to build the plant, which is expected to assemble the Q7, Q8 and Q9. Audi is also expected to announce plans to build 25,000 vehicles in South Carolina, the source added. Audi declined to comment.

item.title: Flávio tem 50,5% dos votos válidos e Lula soma 49,5%, mostra pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão em empate técnico, com vantagem numérica do senador sobre o presidente, mostrou pesquisa BTG/Nexus divulgada neste sábado, véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão em empate técnico, com vantagem numérica do senador sobre o presidente, mostrou pesquisa BTG/Nexus divulgada neste sábado, véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial. Flávio tem 50,5% dos votos válidos, quando não são computados os votos brancos, nulos e os indecisos, contra 49,5% de Lula. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2,2 pontos percentuais para mais e para menos. No primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, Flávio terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. Considerando as intenções de voto totais, o senador soma 47% contra 46% do presidente, segundo a pesquisa deste sábado. No levantamento anterior, no início da semana, o placar era de 46,5% a 45,9% a favor de Flávio. Os que disseram que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum dos dois passaram a 5,2%, ante 4,7%, enquanto os indecisos foram a 1,8%, ante 2,9%. A Nexus ouviu 2.000 eleitores entre sexta-feira e este sábado.

item.title: Hazard winner lifts Lens to 2-1 win over Paris FC
item.description: RC Lens came from behind to beat Paris FC 2-1 on Saturday with Thorgan Hazard’s 83rd-minute winner taking them to within a point of the Ligue 1 leaders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: RC Lens came from behind to beat Paris FC 2-1 on Saturday with Thorgan Hazard’s 83rd-minute winner taking them to within a point of the Ligue 1 leaders. Lens, who were runners-up last season, made a slow start to the season and fired coach Dino Toppmoeller after six matches in charge, but under Yannick Cahuzac they have won successive French league games to advance to 13 points from eight matches. They are one point behind five clubs who share the lead on 14, including Paris FC. Driving rain made it a difficult evening for both sides, with Paris going into the halftime break in the lead despite Lens dominating proceedings. Paris goalkeeper Obed Nkambadio, playing his first game since April, made several saves before a quick counter-attack by his team put them ahead in stoppage time at the end of the first half. A Lens attack was broken up on the edge of Paris’ penalty area and the ball played out to Luca Koleosho, who drove forward and played a one-two with Lassine Sinayoko, before hammering a low right-footed drive into the home net. Lens defender Jean Clair Todibo was shown a red card for a dangerous foul on Ilan Kebbal in the 53rd minute, but it was annulled after VAR found Kebbal had been in an offside position before the challenge. The reprieve was followed by the equaliser from Florian Thauvin, who struck a fine finish from the edge of the area with his left foot and on his 300th Ligue 1 appearance. Hazard volleyed home the winner from Thauvin’s cross as Lens bounced back from losing 3-0 in the Champions League to Belgium’s Club Brugge on Wednesday.

item.title: Valkyries shut down Dream in Game 4 to square WNBA Finals
item.description: ATLANTA -- Discipline and defense were two of the major talking points for Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase entering Game 4 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ATLANTA -- Discipline and defense were two of the major talking points for Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase entering Game 4 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday afternoon. Golden State excelled in both areas and the second-seeded Valkyries earned a pivotal 67-62 victory over the fourth-seeded Atlanta Dream to pull even at two games apiece in the best-of-seven series. Nakase's team, led by Gabby Williams' 17 points, forced 18 Atlanta turnovers and held the Dream to 33.3% shooting from the field. The Valkyries turned over the ball just nine times. "In Game 2 and 3, we kept saying we didn't recognize ourselves," said Nakase, whose team committed 33 turnovers in the two losses. "We took accountability in our film sessions the last two days. Just credit to our players. They're super vulnerable after losses and we get even closer after our losses because we learn from them." Tiffany Hayes and Veronica Burton each scored 13 points for Golden State, which won despite making just four of its 25 3-point attempts. Cecilia Zandalasini had 10 points and Kiah Stokes pulled down 16 rebounds for the Valkyries, who return to San Francisco for Game 5 on Monday. Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 19 points while Jordin Canada and Isobel Borlase chipped in 10 apiece. Angel Reese (eight points) and Allisha Gray (five points) shot a combined 3-for-19 from the field. Reese averaged 25.5 points and 14 rebounds in the Dream's two Finals wins, but was held in check on Saturday. She failed to score in double figures for the first time in this year's playoffs and finished with just nine rebounds. "I think I rushed a lot of my shots," said Reese, who was 2-for-12 with six turnovers on Saturday. "I didn't take my time and finish around the basket the way I've been doing the last three games. It happens. I'm just looking forward to the next game and I'll just be better." Atlanta sliced its 16-point halftime deficit to 46-40 when Borlase made a 3-pointer with 4:27 left in the third quarter. Hayes scored four straight points to extend the visitors' lead to 11 before two Canada free throws narrowed the margin to 54-45 after the third. Consecutive baskets by Howard and Borlase pulled the Dream within six, but Burton responded with a 3-pointer to make it 64-55 at the 4:23 mark of the fourth. From there, two Howard foul shots and Reese's layup cut the deficit to five with 1:36 left. Atlanta had chances to inch closer, but Gray and Borlase missed 3-point attempts before Burton hit a runner on the other end to give the Valkyries a 66-59 advantage with 34.6 seconds remaining. Howard converted a 3-point play, but Burton split a pair of free throws to give Golden State a 67-62 lead. Howard and Canada missed 3-point tries on the next possession to seal the Valkyries' massive win. Nakase trimmed the team's primary rotation as only seven Golden State players recorded 17 minutes or more. Nakase believes her team has the right demeanor to handle changes in playing time on the fly. "We just did what it took to win," Nakase said. "We have ego-less players that understand we're trying to win and we're trying to do what's best for the team. We're about caring for each other, we're about pouring into each other and I think what's been the key is they want to see success in their teammates more than themselves." Borlase made a driving layup to give the Dream a 7-2 edge just over four minutes in. Golden State scored the next 12 points and grabbed a 14-7 lead on Zandalasini's 3-pointer with 2:09 left in the opening quarter. The Valkyries held a 16-11 advantage entering the second quarter despite missing nine of their 10 3-point attempts. After Reese's basket pulled the Dream within four, Golden State rattled off a 9-0 run to extend the lead to 33-20 on Burton's bank with 2:46 left in the half. Kayla Thornton drilled a 3-pointer to push the lead to 16. Williams closed the first half with a layup to put the Valkyries up 42-26. Golden State attempted 40 first-half field goals to Atlanta's 19 as the Valkyries forced the Dream into 14 turnovers in the opening 20 minutes. While Atlanta head coach Karl Smesko appreciated his group's effort to rally, he knows digging a 16-point hole is far from sustainable at this junction of the season. "I was really happy with the fight we showed in the second half, but we can't put ourselves in that position, where you're playing a great defensive team and you're having to come back from double figures," Smesko said. "We're all going to be motivated to come back and have our best game of the series." --Field Level Media

item.title: Inversores de la Generación Z modifican sus carteras antes de las elecciones de medio mandato
item.description: Casi el 75% de los menores de 30 años modificó o evalúa modificar sus inversiones antes de los comicios, frente al 17% de los baby boomers.
item.dc:creator: Zija Song
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Muchos inversores temen que las próximas elecciones legislativas de medio mandato en Estados Unidos sacudan los mercados, pero los de la Generación Z son más propensos que otros a transformar esas preocupaciones en acciones concretas. Casi tres cuartas partes de los inversores de la Generación Z —menores de 30 años— dijeron que modificaron sus carteras antes de las elecciones de noviembre o que estaban considerando hacerlo. Esto sugiere que están realizando cambios a una tasa más de cuatro veces superior a la de los baby boomers, entre quienes el 17% afirmó haber modificado sus inversiones o estar considerando hacerlo, según una encuesta reciente del Nationwide Retirement Institute. Entre los inversores de todos los grupos etarios, el 40% dijo que había realizado cambios. Alrededor del 24% de los encuestados de la Generación Z afirmó que trasladó dinero hacia inversiones más conservadoras o de menor riesgo antes de las elecciones, frente al 13% de los baby boomers. Los inversores más jóvenes también fueron mucho más propensos a diversificar sus carteras con nuevas clases de activos o a consultar a un asesor financiero sobre los riesgos vinculados con las elecciones. La encuesta, realizada en agosto y septiembre por Harris Poll, incluyó a más de 2.000 inversores individuales y 500 profesionales financieros. Si bien algunos movimientos de inversión pueden ser apropiados, otros plantean la posibilidad de que los inversores jóvenes estén tomando decisiones impulsadas por las emociones, que podrían llevarlos a perderse ganancias de los mercados a largo plazo, según asesores financieros y estrategas de mercado. VER MÁS: Jóvenes de Latinoamérica, cada vez más lejos de la independencia económica que tuvieron sus padres El mercado bursátil suele debilitarse antes de la votación y recuperarse una vez que los resultados están definidos. El S&P 500 registró rendimientos positivos en los 12 meses posteriores a todas las elecciones de medio mandato desde 1950, independientemente del partido que resultara ganador, según datos de Bloomberg. El rendimiento promedio del mercado durante esos períodos de 12 meses fue del 15%, frente al rendimiento anual histórico promedio del S&P 500, ligeramente superior al 10%. A menos de tres semanas de las elecciones legislativas del 3 de noviembre, los estadounidenses enfrentan incertidumbre tanto en su vida política como financiera. Aunque los republicanos controlan la Casa Blanca y ambas cámaras del Congreso, las encuestas sugieren que los demócratas probablemente obtengan el control de la Cámara de Representantes y quizá también del Senado. La economía es el principal tema de preocupación para los votantes: más de ocho de cada diez la consideran muy importante al momento de decidir su voto, según el Pew Research Center. Si bien la economía estadounidense continúa creciendo, la persistencia de la inflación, impulsada por el aumento de los costos de la atención médica y de la gasolina, ha debilitado la confianza de los consumidores, que recientemente alcanzó su nivel más bajo desde 2014. La inquietud atraviesa a todas las generaciones. Más de la mitad de los inversores encuestados por Nationwide dijeron que las elecciones de medio mandato les generan más ansiedad, y alrededor de tres cuartas partes creen que el resultado podría afectar significativamente sus planes financieros a largo plazo. Sin embargo, los inversores más jóvenes son mucho más propensos a traducir esas preocupaciones en cambios en sus carteras. Mark Hackett, estratega jefe de mercados del grupo de gestión de inversiones de Nationwide, dijo que le sorprendió la magnitud de las diferencias en las reacciones de las distintas generaciones frente a la ansiedad electoral. Atribuye parte de esa brecha a la experiencia. Los baby boomers, que atravesaron el estallido de la burbuja puntocom y la crisis financiera mundial, aprendieron que los mercados finalmente se recuperan, señaló. Los inversores más jóvenes, que llegaron a la edad adulta después de esas crisis y además deben desenvolverse en un entorno de noticias y redes sociales incesantes, quizá no hayan aprendido las mismas lecciones. “Se siente mal, pero el mercado es mucho más resiliente de lo que la gente cree”, afirmó. Entre los más de 500 asesores y profesionales financieros que participaron en la encuesta de Nationwide, casi dos tercios dijeron que la mejor estrategia durante un año electoral era no hacer absolutamente nada. Jason Lilly, fundador de Tenere Wealth Advisors, con sede en Massachusetts, dijo que realizó algunos ajustes en las carteras de sus clientes en las últimas semanas. Consciente de que los mercados pueden volverse volátiles antes de las elecciones, recientemente vendió acciones para clientes que, según sabía, necesitarían efectivo para cubrir sus gastos de manutención o cumplir con los requisitos de retiros anuales obligatorios de cuentas con impuestos diferidos. Sin embargo, más allá de estos ajustes de mantenimiento, aconseja a los inversores mantener sus posiciones. Las semanas en torno a las elecciones “se van a sentir un poco tormentosas”, dijo. “No haría cambios importantes”. Aunque ambos partidos sostienen que gestionan mejor la economía y el mercado bursátil, un estudio de los rendimientos del mercado entre 1950 y 2023 realizado por la firma de corretaje LPL Financial concluyó que los mercados tendían a comportarse mejor cuando los dos partidos se repartían el control de Washington. En los años con un presidente republicano y un Congreso dividido —uno de los escenarios posibles para noviembre—, las acciones registraron rendimientos promedio de casi el 14%. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los estrategas de mercado señaló que el reducido tamaño de las muestras dificulta extraer conclusiones definitivas. VER MÁS: La Generación Z prefiere no salir con nadie antes que gastar US$250 en una cena y tragos “Hay muchísimas otras cosas que van a determinar los precios del mercado”, dijo Wes Crill, vicepresidente de Dimensional Fund Advisors, una de las mayores gestoras de fondos. A largo plazo, “independientemente de quién haya estado en la Casa Blanca o en el Congreso, los rendimientos han sido positivos”.

item.title: Gastos de lujo de los pasajeros más adinerados salvan a las aerolíneas de un desplome de márgenes
item.description: Las aerolíneas refuerzan su apuesta por los viajes de lujo mientras el combustible caro presiona sus márgenes. La demanda de asientos prémium se mantiene firme, incluso con tarifas aéreas en alza.
item.dc:creator: Sri Taylor, Kate Duffy
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Robert Doornbos gastó el año pasado más dinero en vuelos que lo que gana anualmente el estadounidense promedio, pero el expiloto de Fórmula 1 dijo que es su manera de recuperar tiempo. Doornbos, que vive en Dubái, contó que realizó unos 50 vuelos en clase ejecutiva el año pasado. Está dispuesto a soportar tarifas aéreas más elevadas —como los €7.500 (US$8.407) que pagó por un pasaje a Madrid para asistir a un Gran Premio— a cambio de la comodidad de llegar descansado y listo para trabajar. “Intento minimizar la pérdida de tiempo”, dijo Doornbos, que ahora trabaja como orador en eventos. “Vuelo mucho, pero de una manera eficiente”. Precisamente, Doornbos es el tipo de cliente que tienen en mente las mayores aerolíneas del mundo mientras profundizan su apuesta por los viajes de lujo. Las compañías confían en que los pasajeros adinerados seguirán gastando grandes sumas en asientos costosos, incluso cuando las tarifas aéreas se disparan. Solo en las últimas semanas, British Airways presentó la cabina de clase ejecutiva más grande del mercado; Delta Air Lines Inc. anunció que está cerca de duplicar su flota de automóviles Porsche AG que trasladan a sus clientes más fieles entre los aviones y las terminales aeroportuarias; e incluso Southwest Airlines Co., que históricamente se caracterizó por mantener los costos bajos, está incorporando opciones prémium. Los precios de los pasajes aéreos en Estados Unidos aumentaron un 22% en septiembre respecto del mismo mes del año anterior, según datos de la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales. Sin embargo, los ejecutivos de las aerolíneas afirman que la demanda de sus asientos más caros apenas se ha debilitado, mientras los viajeros más sensibles a los precios enfrentan una presión cada vez mayor. VER MÁS : Aeropuertos Argentina emitió obligaciones negociables por US$ 400 millones al 8% “Si observamos al 40% de los clientes que más gastan, acumularon más de US$40 billones en riqueza durante los últimos años”, dijo Ed Bastian, director ejecutivo de Delta, en una entrevista previa a la presentación de los resultados del tercer trimestre. “Tienen los recursos, están dando prioridad a los viajes y estos ocupan un lugar destacado en su lista”. La demanda de los consumidores está proporcionando un salvavidas crucial a una industria que enfrenta un aumento de los costos del combustible y una reducción de los márgenes de ganancias como consecuencia de una guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán que no muestra señales de terminar. Los analistas esperan que los precios de la energía se mantengan elevados, lo que prolongaría la presión financiera sobre las aerolíneas de todo el mundo. El presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, dijo que los combates podrían terminar después de las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato de noviembre. Las aerolíneas sostienen que la actividad subyacente es sólida, pero que los elevados precios del combustible están perjudicando sus resultados. Delta, una de las compañías con mejor desempeño del sector, redujo recientemente sus previsiones de ganancias para todo el año. Más adelante esta semana, se espera que United Airlines Holdings Inc., American Airlines Group Inc. y Southwest presenten proyecciones igualmente moderadas. Delta afirmó que, por primera vez en la historia de la aviación comercial, los ingresos trimestrales por pasajes prémium superaron las ventas de la clase económica tradicional. La demanda de las opciones prémium continúa sin mostrar señales de desaceleración. Eric Gentry, de 65 años y cofundador de Jet Set Natural, un suplemento herbal para tratar el desfase horario, acepta pagar tarifas más altas porque viajar es una de sus formas favoritas de disfrutar el tiempo libre. Durante el último año, visitó Ciudad de México, Sicilia y Carolina del Sur. “Si los viajes aéreos aumentan considerablemente de precio, uno puede recortar un poco los gastos en hoteles, alojamiento y actividades en el destino”, dijo. “De una forma u otra, hay que llegar. Así que, si uno quiere ir a un lugar, absorbe el costo”. Las aerolíneas están destinando grandes inversiones a sus cabinas más rentables y transformando lo que antes era una forma cómoda de viajar en una experiencia similar a la de un hotel de lujo a 10.600 metros de altura. La reciente renovación de la clase ejecutiva Delta One incluye hamburguesas de carne wagyu, bourbon Blanton’s de barrica única, champán Taittinger y vinos que pueden venderse a más de US$200 la botella. La compañía también está incorporando almohadas de Missoni y ampliando su flota de vehículos Porsche para los traslados prémium en los aeropuertos. VER MÁS: Aerolíneas Argentinas volvió a registrar pérdidas por la suba del precio del combustible “Es muy importante invertir de manera constante en experiencias prémium porque los clientes tienen opciones y, sin importar el contexto, hay que ganarse su preferencia y su dinero”, dijo Ranjan Goswami, director de marketing y producto de Delta. La apuesta por la parte delantera del avión va más allá de Estados Unidos. La renovación de los Airbus A380 de dos pisos de British Airways, prevista para finales de este año, ofrecerá más asientos en clase ejecutiva para captar la demanda “muy resiliente” de viajes prémium, afirmó Luis Gallego, director ejecutivo de IAG. Por su parte, la competidora Air France-KLM recibió recientemente un premio a la mejor primera clase del mundo en la clasificación anual de aerolíneas de Skytrax. La carrera por mejorar las cabinas ha afectado a algunas compañías, entre ellas Deutsche Lufthansa AG, que sufrió demoras en la certificación de sus asientos Allegris. Esto obligó a la aerolínea a operar nuevos Boeing 787 Dreamliner con gran parte de las áreas de clase ejecutiva aisladas. “En el pasado, la clase económica se agotaba primero porque la gente priorizaba el precio, mientras que los asientos de primera clase y clase ejecutiva seguían disponibles hasta pocos días antes de la salida”, dijo el director ejecutivo de Lufthansa, Carsten Spohr, durante un encuentro con los medios. “Ahora ocurre lo contrario: primero se agotan la primera clase, la clase ejecutiva y la económica prémium”. Incluso Southwest, conocida durante mucho tiempo por su enfoque sin lujos, busca atraer a clientes dispuestos a pagar más. Tony Roach, director de experiencia del cliente y marca de la aerolínea, dijo el jueves a Bloomberg que “agregar opciones prémium busca ampliar su atractivo, no abandonar a su clientela tradicional. Viajar es una de las grandes pasiones de la gente”. A esta tendencia se suman las declaraciones de Bastian y otros ejecutivos, quienes sostienen que las tarifas aéreas más elevadas no disuadirán a quienes aman viajar. Gentry es uno de esos clientes. Está organizando un viaje a un destino cálido para pasar unas vacaciones en la playa y ya hizo algunas concesiones: eligió Miami en lugar del Caribe porque era un poco más barato. Según explicó, es flexible respecto del destino, pero viajar es la prioridad. “No creo que vaya a viajar menos”, dijo Gentry. “Lo que haré será ajustar el presupuesto, especialmente si quiero mantener la frecuencia de mis viajes”. Lea más en Bloomberg.

item.title: Ravens change course, rule out QB Lamar Jackson vs. Bengals
item.description: Lamar Jackson practiced and said he was ready to return from a two-week absence caused by a high-ankle sprain, but the Ravens are going a different direction against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson practiced and said he was ready to return from a two-week absence caused by a high-ankle sprain, but the Ravens are going a different direction against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. Baltimore downgraded Jackson to out on Saturday afternoon, less than 24 hours before the AFC North rivals collide in Cincinnati. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley, 1-1 this season subbing for Jackson, gets the call for his third consecutive start. "I just know it was a sprain, and it hurt bad," Jackson said of the injury to reporters on Friday. "It was very, very, very, very, very painful." The Ravens are one of three 4-2 teams in the AFC North and lead the division in points (156) while ranking last in points allowed (132). Baltimore has 116 points and 14 touchdowns with Jackson at quarterback this season, compared to 40 points and four touchdowns without him. Jackson is 11-2 in his career against the Bengals. --Field Level Media

item.title: Teck says strike begins at Highland Valley Copper mine in British Columbia
item.description: Teck Resources said on Saturday workers had started a strike at its Highland Valley Copper mine in British Columbia, with operations continuing at reduced capacity.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Teck Resources (TECKb.TO) said on Saturday workers had started a strike at its Highland Valley Copper mine in British Columbia, with operations continuing at reduced capacity. Here are some details: The impact on overall production remains dependent on the duration of the strike, Teck said The labour action follows the expiry of a 72-hour notice served by United Steelworkers (USW) Local 7619 after contract talks [USN:L4N4671NC TEXT:"failed"] to produce a new collective agreement The United Steelworkers union represents about 1,200 workers at Highland Valley, according to its website In its strike notice, the union said it is seeking higher wages and improved pensions, arguing the mine faces challenges attracting and retaining skilled workers amid staffing shortages Teck said it remains committed to negotiating a new collective agreement The USW did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Tristan Luneau pushes Ducks past resurgent Flyers
item.description: Tristan Luneau had a goal and two assists as the visiting Anaheim Ducks snapped a five-game losing streak with a 5-4 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tristan Luneau had a goal and two assists as the visiting Anaheim Ducks snapped a five-game losing streak with a 5-4 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers on Saturday. Leo Carlsson chipped in with a goal and an assist against the team that signed him to a five-year, $90 million offer sheet over the summer. Anaheim ultimately matched the deal, making the 21-year-old the highest paid player in the league. Matvei Michkov scored his seventh and eighth goals for Philadelphia, which had won three straight since losing its first nine contests. Porter Martone and Tyson Foerster also scored for the Flyers, while Trevor Zegras recorded two assists against his former team. The Ducks took a 5-3 lead with two goals early in the third period. The go-ahead tally was Luneau's first of the season on a seemingly harmless shot that snuck past Joseph Woll. Beckett Sennecke then created a two-goal lead when he tipped home a feed from Carlsson for a power-play goal. Just over a minute later, Michkov poked in a loose puck to bring the Flyers within 5-4. Philadelphia never seriously threatened down the stretch, despite getting a power play for the final 40.7 seconds. Anaheim's Sam Colangelo and A.J. Greer took simultaneous minor penalties with 6:19 left in the first period -- a sequence that led to two Philadelphia goals. Michkov scored first on a shot through traffic with the Flyers skating 5-on-3, and then Martone scored on a great setup from Travis Sanheim on the ensuing 5-on-4. The Ducks got on the board midway through the second period, as Cutter Gauthier stole the puck behind the net and found Carlsson for a goal. Greer tied it less than five minutes later, but the Flyers answered right back. Foerster gave the hosts a 3-2 lead with a short-handed goal against Lukas Dostal. But the visitors responded just over a minute later as Judd Caulfield tipped in a centering pass by Alex Killorn to create a 3-3 tie. Anaheim received a power play late in the second period, but Woll held firm with back-to-back terrific saves against Gauthier. Woll finished with 21 saves for the Flyers, while Dostal turned aside 28 shots for the Ducks. --Field Level Media

item.title: Fato ou Fake não classificou 41 falas de Flávio em debate como falsas
item.description: O Fato ou Fake, serviço de checagem de fatos do Grupo Globo, não classificou como falsas 41 declarações feitas pelo candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no debate eleitoral com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) promovido pela emissora na última sexta-feira, a dois dias do segundo turno do pleito de 2026.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: O Fato ou Fake, serviço de checagem de fatos do Grupo Globo, não classificou como falsas 41 declarações feitas pelo candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no debate eleitoral com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) promovido pela emissora na última sexta-feira, a dois dias do segundo turno do pleito de 2026. “A TV Globo exibiu uma checagem de falas e os números chamaram atenção. O quadro Fato ou Fake comparou declarações de Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula. A postagem destaca a diferença entre os resultados apresentados”, diz um post no Instagram que associa o número à checagem do Grupo Globo. A publicação reproduz uma parte do Jornal da Globo , exibido após o debate, na qual as jornalistas Andréia Sadi e Renata Lo Prete mencionam uma fala de Flávio checada pelo Fato ou Fake. O trecho pode ser visto aos 25 minutos do jornal. O conteúdo checado diz que o Fato ou Fake considerou 41 declarações de Flávio como falsas, contra apenas uma de Lula. No entanto, somados os dois candidatos, o site checou 37 alegações durante o debate. O Fato ou Fake segue uma metodologia própria e classifica as declarações checadas de três formas: “Fato”, “Não é bem assim” e “Fake”. No caso de Flávio, a página sinalizou 5 falas como “Fato”, 4 como “Não é bem assim” e 9 como “Fake”. Já para Lula foram 11 como “Fato”, 5 como “Não é bem assim” e 3 como “Fake”. VEREDICTO Enganoso. O Fato ou Fake não apontou que Flávio fez 41 declarações falsas durante o debate na Globo, mas 9. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: La policía de París usa gases lacrimógenos y cañones de agua para dispersar a manifestantes
item.description: La policía francesa utilizó gases lacrimógenos y un cañón de agua en París tras una jornada de protestas que reunió a 410.000 personas en todo el país y dejó unas 1.000 detenciones.
item.dc:creator: James Regan, Benoit Berthelot
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La policía utilizó gases lacrimógenos y un cañón de agua para dispersar a las multitudes en París después de que decenas de miles de personas marcharan en su mayoría pacíficamente el sábado para protestar por el alto costo de vida y la insuficiente financiación de las escuelas. Los enfrentamientos al final de la jornada reflejaron las tensiones registradas en otras ciudades francesas, entre ellas Lyon y Burdeos. En Grenoble, cerca de 400 personas encapuchadas vestidas de negro atacaron a las fuerzas de seguridad y causaron daños a propiedades, según las autoridades regionales. Unas 2.000 personas hicieron lo mismo en París, según el ministro del Interior, Laurent Nuñez. Unas 410.000 personas se manifestaron en toda Francia, incluidas unas 110.000 en la capital, informó el Ministerio del Interior, lo que indica una menor participación que el fin de semana anterior. El Gobierno francés había dicho que planeaba desplegar 70.000 efectivos de seguridad, incluidas fuerzas de élite antiterroristas, para evitar que se repitieran la violencia y los saqueos registrados en todo el país una semana antes, que tomaron desprevenidas a las fuerzas de seguridad. “Las marchas transcurrieron bien”, dijo Nuñez a periodistas el sábado por la noche. “Deberíamos estar agradecidos de que se haya podido ejercer la libertad de expresión, pero lamentar que un número de personas estuviera allí con un único objetivo: hacer que las marchas degeneraran”. VER MÁS: Francia desplegará militares para contener nuevas protestas este fin de semana Muchos manifestantes llevaban banderas sindicales y carteles en los que criticaban a la policía y al Gobierno del presidente Emmanuel Macron. Grupos estudiantiles y sindicatos convocaron a nuevas manifestaciones hasta que el Gobierno abandone su plan presupuestario y aumente el gasto en servicios públicos. Cuando la marcha llegaba a su fin bajo la lluvia en el este de París, varios grupos —a menudo con cascos o capuchas negras, gafas y máscaras— se enfrentaron a la policía. En Nantes, en el oeste de Francia, la policía utilizó un cañón de agua para impedir que algunas personas ingresaran a un lugar donde las protestas estaban prohibidas. Las manifestaciones nacionales de la semana pasada congregaron a más de medio millón de personas y se tornaron violentas cuando grupos de alborotadores atacaron edificios públicos y entraron por la fuerza en comercios de todo el país, incluida París, se enfrentaron con la policía y prendieron fuego a automóviles. “Una vez más hoy, las fuerzas de seguridad se enfrentaron a un nivel extremadamente alto de violencia”, dijo Nuñez. “Gracias a la intervención de las fuerzas del orden, se evitaron muchos actos de saqueo. Gracias a la intervención de las fuerzas del orden, no hubo ataques dirigidos contra edificios públicos, como ocurrió el 17 de octubre”. Agregó que se habían producido unas 1.000 detenciones y dijo que esperaba que la cifra aumentara significativamente. Las autoridades de París restringieron la principal marcha del sábado al extremo sureste de la ciudad, entre Porte d’Italie y Porte de Vincennes, evitando las rutas más tradicionales por el centro. La policía, mediante altavoces, ordenó previamente a la gente despejar la Place de la Bastille, conocida como el lugar de nacimiento de la Revolución Francesa de 1789, desde donde se había previsto que comenzara la manifestación. VER MÁS: Bardella es reelegido presidente de Agrupación Nacional, partido francés de extrema derecha Los comercios de París, incluidas muchas boutiques de lujo, tapiaron sus ventanas y contrataron personal de seguridad adicional, mientras que algunos cerraron por completo. Tres atracciones populares —el Louvre, el Museo de Orsay y el Museo Picasso— permanecieron cerradas el sábado, y un partido de fútbol programado entre Paris Saint-Germain y Olympique Lyonnais en París fue aplazado. Sin embargo, algunas zonas de París funcionaron con normalidad el sábado. La ciudad y la National Football League organizaron un evento “Hail Mary” a orillas del Sena, junto a la catedral de Notre-Dame, antes del partido del domingo entre New Orleans y Pittsburgh. Los aficionados que viajaban en barcos turísticos por el río pasaban ondeando pompones dorados sobre sus cabezas y vistiendo camisetas negras, los colores de ambos equipos. La emblemática Torre Eiffel de la ciudad también permaneció abierta. Soldados ayudaban a proteger edificios sensibles. También estaban disponibles helicópteros y vehículos blindados conocidos como Centaurs. Algunas ciudades, entre ellas Lyon, prohibieron las protestas el sábado y ampliaron los toques de queda. Macron reconoció el jueves “fallas en la planificación y elementos de sorpresa” detrás de los acontecimientos del fin de semana pasado. El mandatario francés, que aplazó una gira por África occidental prevista para la próxima semana, responsabilizó a grupos de extrema izquierda por lo que calificó como actos sediciosos. Según el alcalde de París, Emmanuel Grégoire, había indicios en las redes sociales de que grupos de hooligans también planeaban concentrarse en la capital francesa la próxima semana. “Nos estamos preparando para una situación de largo plazo, durante varias semanas”, dijo al diario Le Parisien, y estimó que el costo para el Ayuntamiento podría ascender a decenas de millones de euros. VER MÁS : Los disturbios disparan las ventas de armas de autodefensa en las ciudades más afectadas de Francia Respaldadas por un grupo heterogéneo de figuras de las redes sociales, estudiantes, sindicatos y partidos de izquierda, las manifestaciones del sábado fueron presentadas como un “Acte II”, o segunda ronda, del movimiento de protesta. Buena parte del enojo está dirigido contra Macron, cuya popularidad se ha desplomado seis meses antes del final de su segundo mandato. El movimiento todavía cuenta con el apoyo de una mayoría de la población, según una encuesta de Cluster 17 realizada para L’Opinion entre 3.000 adultos del 19 al 22 de octubre, aunque su respaldo cayó 4 puntos, al 53%. Al mismo tiempo, el 59% de los encuestados quiere que termine rápidamente, 6 puntos más que en la medición anterior, mientras aumentan las preocupaciones por las consecuencias económicas y sociales. Las encuestas muestran que la violencia ha beneficiado a la candidata de extrema derecha Marine Le Pen, favorita para las elecciones presidenciales de abril. El sábado reunió a sus seguidores en Orleans para el congreso de su partido, Agrupación Nacional, mientras miles de sus opositores, incluidos dirigentes de izquierda y sindicales, participaron en una marcha de protesta en la ciudad del centro de Francia. Una encuesta de Ipsos-BVA-Cési École d’ingénieurs para Le Parisien, publicada el sábado, mostró que, aunque Le Pen mantiene una ventaja clara, el líder de la izquierda radical de La Francia Insumisa, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, también se ha beneficiado de las protestas y ocupa el segundo lugar, por delante de varios competidores de centro. La encuesta, realizada en línea entre 1.500 adultos, se llevó a cabo el 21 y 22 de octubre. La agitación ha incrementado los temores sobre las finanzas públicas. Aunque Francia evitó una rebaja de calificación por parte de Moody’s Ratings el viernes por la noche, el país enfrenta dificultades para reducir el déficit presupuestario antes de las elecciones de 2027. Un indicador muy seguido del riesgo de los bonos aumentó hasta niveles no vistos desde la crisis de deuda de la zona euro: el diferencial entre los rendimientos de los bonos franceses y alemanes a 10 años, considerados el activo de refugio de la región, alcanzó los 178 puntos básicos el jueves, frente a apenas 85 puntos básicos a comienzos de septiembre. La actividad económica del sector privado también se contrajo este mes, con el Índice de Gerentes de Compras compuesto elaborado por S&P Global cayendo a 48,4 en octubre desde 51,1 el mes anterior. El indicador se ubicó así por debajo del umbral de 50 puntos que separa la expansión de la contracción. Siguen apareciendo indicios del impacto. El sábado, el director ejecutivo de Breitling dijo que la marca suiza de relojes de lujo se preparaba para un golpe en las ventas de la temporada de fin de año debido a que los turistas se mantienen alejados de París. Francia no es el único país europeo que enfrenta protestas. En Tirana estallaron enfrentamientos el sábado, cuando manifestantes que exigían la renuncia del primer ministro albanés, Edi Rama, arrojaron piedras y provocaron incendios, mientras la policía respondió con gases lacrimógenos, cañones de agua y balas de goma. VER MÁS: Entrevista al embajador argentino en Francia: el encuentro entre Milei y Bernard Arnault y “Argentina cruzó un rubicón” En Italia, la policía utilizó gases lacrimógenos en Turín después de que manifestantes arrojaran adoquines y botellas, según la agencia de noticias Ansa. También hubo enfrentamientos con la policía en Roma y Bolonia. En Milán, donde las protestas derivaron en saqueos la semana pasada, las autoridades bloquearon el acceso a la céntrica Piazza del Duomo. Aun así, unos 10.000 manifestantes se congregaron en Milán, informó Corriere della Sera. También hubo protestas en Bélgica. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Spurs celebrate ending Chelsea hoodoo with 2-0 win
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur's 2-0 win at London rivals Chelsea – only their second at Stamford Bridge since Margaret Thatcher was Britain’s prime minister – was greeted by their coach, players and fans as a turning point in their season.
item.dc:creator: William Schomberg
item.content:encoded: Tottenham Hotspur's 2-0 win at London rivals Chelsea – only their second at Stamford Bridge since Margaret Thatcher was Britain’s prime minister – was greeted by their coach, players and fans as a turning point in their season. Roberto De Zerbi's men were bottom of the Premier League before they beat fellow strugglers Coventry City 3-1 at home on Monday and Saturday’s victory propelled them to 12th place pending the rest of the weekend’s fixtures. The north Londoners had won once in their previous 41 visits to Chelsea in all competitions - a run stretching back to February 1990 when Gary Lineker scored the winning goal. Their only previous win at Chelsea during that 36-year drought was a 3-1 victory in 2018. No wonder the away fans celebrated at the final whistle as if they had just won a trophy and the Spurs players could be heard from the Stamford Bridge press room jumping up and down in the changing room still wearing their boots. "I think we are playing well, not just today," De Zerbi told BBC Radio once the celebrations abated. "Maybe now there is another atmosphere, there is another union amongst the players. With these two wins in a row they can believe more and more in themselves," the Italian said before later telling reporters: "We have suffered enough." There was a touch of luck to the result - the match seemed to be heading to a 0-0 stalemate before Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders, on his full Premier League debut, punched the ball into his own net from a Matheus Fernandes corner. Spurs made sure of the win with a breakaway strike by Mathys Tel 10 minutes later. "It's very special because we have come to Chelsea so many times and not got a win," the French striker told Sky Sports. "We showed great mentality today and we need to enjoy this win." In between the goals, Chelsea playmaker Cole Palmer was sent off for the first time in his senior career when he was booked twice in nine minutes. Spurs dominated possession with 70% of the ball over the match and 15 shots to Chelsea's seven. The Blues, who remain fourth in the table ahead of Sunday's matches, looked far from their fluent best and missed the focal point of top scorer Joao Pedro who was injured in training on Friday and is due to undergo tests in the coming days. "We need to be self-critical. We need to be at a better level," Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso told the BBC. "Sometimes you feel good and today, collectively and individually, we were not at our best." Asked about Palmer picking up two yellow cards in quick succession, Alonso said he wanted to see more self-control among his players, who last season racked up eight reds. "In those situations, the first yellow card can be decisive," the Spaniard said. "It’s a process of the maturity of the team and of the individual players as well."

item.title: Hamilton es el más rápido y completa barrida de Ferrari en entrenamientos del Gran Premio de EEUU
item.description: Lewis Hamilton fue el más rápido con Ferrari en la última sesión de entrenamientos del Gran Premio de Estados Unidos celebrada el sábado, después de que su compañero de equipo, Charles Leclerc, liderara las dos rondas del viernes en el Circuito de las Américas de Austin.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Lewis Hamilton fue el más rápido con Ferrari en la última sesión de entrenamientos del Gran Premio de Estados Unidos celebrada el sábado, después de que su compañero de equipo, Charles Leclerc, liderara las dos rondas del viernes en el Circuito de las Américas de Austin. El siete veces campeón del mundo había quedado por detrás de Leclerc el viernes y se había quejado de los baches y de la configuración de su monoplaza. El piloto de 41 años marcó un mejor tiempo de un minuto y 34,893 segundos, 0,168 más rápido que el Red Bull de Max Verstappen, y 0,234 más rápido que Leclerc, completando así la barrida de Ferrari en los entrenamientos de cara a la clasificación que tendrá lugar más tarde el sábado. Leclerc habría sido el más rápido si no le hubieran anulado su mejor vuelta por sobrepasarse los límites de la pista en la curva nueve, mientras que Hamilton también tuvo que realizar una maniobra evasiva en una vuelta rápida al final de la sesión para esquivar al Audi de Gabriel Bortoleto. El líder del campeonato Kimi Antonelli, que puede hacerse con el título con Mercedes el domingo si gana y los resultados le son favorables, fue quinto —perdiendo también un tiempo de vuelta por superar los límites de la pista—, mientras que su rival más cercano y compañero de equipo, George Russell, quedó cuarto. Antonelli aventaja a Russell por 102 puntos a falta de cinco carreras tras Austin, a menos que las dos últimas en Oriente Medio tengan que cancelarse debido al conflicto en la región. El cuatro veces campeón del mundo Verstappen ha ganado las dos últimas carreras en Malasia y Singapur, y también se impuso desde la pole en Austin la temporada pasada. Oscar Piastri, de McLaren, fue sexto, mientras que su compañero de equipo y actual campeón, Lando Norris, quedó octavo. Nico Hülkenberg, de Audi, se situó entre ambos. Pierre Gasly, de Alpine, e Isack Hadjar, de Red Bull, completaron los 10 primeros puestos.

item.title: A’ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart headline All-WNBA teams
item.description: Las Vegas' A'ja Wilson and New York's Breanna Stewart headline the 2026 All-WNBA teams, as announced by the league on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las Vegas' A'ja Wilson and New York's Breanna Stewart headline the 2026 All-WNBA teams, as announced by the league on Saturday. Indiana's Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell as well as Minnesota's Olivia Miles join Wilson and Stewart on the first-team roster. A five-time MVP for the Aces, Wilson had another impressive season in 2026, boasting averages of 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds and 3.2 assists as Las Vegas went 31-13 with a semifinals appearance. This is her seventh All-WNBA selection. Stewart, a two-time MVP, averaged 20.8 points and 8.3 rebounds for the 26-18 Liberty, good enough to earn her an eighth appearance on the All-WNBA team. Clark and Mitchell teamed to improve the Fever's fortunes in 2026, boosting the team to a 28-16 finish. Mitchell scored a team-leading 24.7 points per game while Clark chipped in 22.3 points and 8.3 assists as her backcourt mate. It is Clark's second All-WNBA appearance as well as Mitchell's. Miles helped power the Lynx to the league's best record (33-11) as a rookie. She was recognized with an All-Star appearance while averaging 19.8 points, 4.7 rebounds and 6.0 assists. The All-WNBA second team includes Washington's Shakira Austin, Dallas' Paige Bueckers, Atlanta's Rhyne Howard and Angel Reese and Las Vegas' Jackie Young. Those are the first All-WNBA selections for Austin, Reese and Howard. It is Bueckers' second selection and Young's third. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hombres armados matan al menos a 40 personas en el noreste de Nigeria: Amnistía Internacional
item.description: Hombres armados mataron al menos a 40 personas en un ataque perpetrado el viernes por la tarde en una aldea del estado de Taraba, en el noreste de Nigeria, informó Amnistía Internacional.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Kingimi, Adewale Kolawole
item.content:encoded: Hombres armados mataron al menos a 40 personas en un ataque perpetrado el viernes por la tarde en una aldea del estado de Taraba, en el noreste de Nigeria, informó Amnistía Internacional. Un numeroso grupo de hombres armados llevó a cabo el ataque contra la aldea de Binnari, informó la policía en un comunicado el sábado. AI señaló en un comunicado que, aunque la policía había confirmado inicialmente la muerte de 10 personas, el sábado se recuperaron más cadáveres. Los atacantes irrumpieron en la aldea con disparos y saquearon alimentos de las tiendas, informó la policía. El norte de Nigeria ha sufrido un recrudecimiento de los ataques perpetrados por bandas criminales fuertemente armadas, que asaltan aldeas, secuestran a los residentes para pedir rescate y roban ganado.

item.title: Report: Yankees running it back with pitching coach Matt Blake
item.description: It was not a banner year for the New York Yankees, but the organization appears prepared to stay with the same coaching group for 2027. In their latest move, the Yankees have agreed to sign pitching coach Matt Blake to a three-year contract extension, according to the New York Post.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: It was not a banner year for the New York Yankees, but the organization appears prepared to stay with the same coaching group for 2027. In their latest move, the Yankees have agreed to sign pitching coach Matt Blake to a three-year contract extension, according to the New York Post. Blake's extension comes on the heels of the Yankees retaining manager Aaron Boone and general manager Brian Cashman. New York had the American League's highest payroll ($310 million) last season, but did not make it past the AL Division Series for the second year in a row. The Yankees' 2026 season ended in disappointment, as New York (93-68) finished 4-1/2 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East and then were swept in the playoffs by the Rays. Blake, for his part, seemed to hold up his end of the bargain, overseeing a staff that included Cy Young contender Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA) and an effective return from Gerrit Cole (10-9, 3.61). Will Warren gave the group a third 10-game winner (11-6, 3.92), but Max Fried (5-5, 2.80) and Carlos Rodon (7-3, 2.67) missed large chunks of the season due to injury. The Yankees finished first in the majors with a 3.23 team ERA under the 41-year-old Blake, who has been the team's pitching coach since the 2020 season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lakers, Walker Kessler put undefeated start up against Jazz
item.description: Walker Kessler is thriving after two games with the Los Angeles Lakers and will get a chance to show off his form against his former team, the Utah Jazz, on Sunday at Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Walker Kessler is thriving after two games with the Los Angeles Lakers and will get a chance to show off his form against his former team, the Utah Jazz, on Sunday at Salt Lake City. A shakeup in the starting lineup got the Jazz in the win column Friday and may prove beneficial going forward as Utah continues to search for a flow following Kessler's departure. The Jazz edged the New Orleans Pelicans 120-119 on Friday after Jaxson Hayes gave the Jazz a spark off the bench. Hayes, who played for the Lakers the past three seasons, started Utah's season-opening loss at Memphis on Wednesday before moving to the second unit against the Pelicans. Hayes scored 17 points with five rebounds in 26 minutes and defended the rim well while hitting big baskets to key a fourth-quarter rally. "I think Jaxson at the five creates a different set of matchups for us offensively, which will maybe have us see a few different coverages, potentially give us some more space with that first group," Jazz coach Will Hardy said. Utah did struggle to play a consistent 48 minutes. A poor third quarter nearly doomed the effort as the Jazz blew a 15-point lead while committing eight turnovers and seven fouls in the period. The Pelicans also shot 60.9% from the floor in the third quarter. Jaren Jackson Jr., who finished with a team-high 24 points and 10 rebounds, stepped up in the fourth quarter along with Hayes to prevent an 0-2 start. Now comes the reunion with Kessler after the Jazz dealt the big man to Los Angeles over the summer in exchange for a pair of unprotected first-round draft picks and two first-round pick swaps. It was a steep price tag for Kessler, who played only five games last season because of a shoulder injury. The Lakers saw him as an essential component of their future as they sought to retool their roster around Luka Doncic after LeBron James' departure. So far, Kessler has lived up to expectations. Kessler has averaged 24 points on 84.6% shooting, 8.5 rebounds, and four blocks in his first two games with the Lakers. He had 22 points, six blocks, and three steals to help lead the Lakers to a 125-117 victory over the Clippers -- their ninth win in 13 meetings with their crosstown rivals. Kessler became the eighth Laker player all time to tally six blocks and three steals in a single game. "It's kind of crazy that there have been seven guys who have done it before," Kessler said. "I know there's some absolute legends in the Lakers franchise -- definitely an honor." The Lakers pulled away from the Clippers in the third quarter after a tight first half due to Kessler's defensive dominance. "(He) really was a huge spark for us getting this win," Lakers head coach JJ Redick said. "There were multiple times where it felt like they had a layup and he either came over and blocked the shot or created an altered shot." Los Angeles swept the season series against Utah last season by winning all four games. The Lakers are 7-1 against the Jazz over the past two seasons. --Field Level Media

item.title: Gunmen kill at least 40 people in northeastern Nigeria, Amnesty International says
item.description: Gunmen killed at least 40 people in an attack on a village in Nigeria's northeastern Taraba state on Friday afternoon, Amnesty International said.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Kingimi, Adewale Kolawole
item.content:encoded: Gunmen killed at least 40 people in an attack on a village in Nigeria's northeastern Taraba state on Friday afternoon, Amnesty International said. A large group of gunmen carried out the attack on Binnari village, police said in a statement on Saturday Amnesty International said in a statement that while police had earlier confirmed the killing of 10 people, more bodies were recovered later on Saturday The attackers invaded the village with heavy gunfire and looted food items from shops, police said Northern Nigeria has experienced a surge in [USN:L8N45T13I TEXT:"attacks"] by heavily armed criminal gangs, known locally as bandits, who raid villages, abduct residents for ransom and steal livestock

item.title: Cooper Flagg (shoulder) out vs. Spurs, to be reevaluated next week
item.description: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg will miss Saturday's home game against the San Antonio Spurs because of a mild left shoulder sprain.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg will miss Saturday's home game against the San Antonio Spurs because of a mild left shoulder sprain. Flagg, last season's NBA Rookie of the Year, left the Mavericks' 121-105 victory over the Indiana Pacers on Friday following a hard collision with Aaron Nesmith one minute before halftime. Alone on a fastbreak, Flagg went up for a two-handed dunk when Nesmith committed a flagrant foul. Mavericks head coach Dusty May said postgame that Flagg was in "good spirits" in the locker room. The 19-year-old, who scored 14 points with six assists in 17 minutes, underwent an MRI on Saturday that diagnosed the injury and he will be reevaluated next week. Flagg delivered 32 points, five rebounds, two assists, three steals and one block in his lone full game this season, a 128-110 loss to the Houston Rockets on Wednesday. After playing host to the Spurs, Dallas faces the Miami Heat on the road Monday before returning home for six of its next seven games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hamilton fastest to complete Ferrari's US Grand Prix practice sweep
item.description: Lewis Hamilton was fastest for Ferrari in final practice for the US Grand Prix on Saturday after teammate Charles Leclerc led Friday's two sessions at Austin's Circuit of the Americas.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Lewis Hamilton was fastest for Ferrari in final practice for the US Grand Prix on Saturday after teammate Charles Leclerc [USN:L6N4691A0 TEXT:"led Friday's two sessions"] at Austin's Circuit of the Americas. The seven-time world champion had trailed Leclerc a day earlier, complaining about the bumps and the set-up direction of his upgraded car, but he seemed to have got it back to what he wanted. The 41-year-old lapped in a best time of one minute 34.893 seconds, 0.168 quicker than Red Bull rival Max Verstappen and 0.234 faster than Leclerc, to complete the Ferrari practice sweep ahead of Saturday's qualifying, with Ferrari chasing a first pole of 2026. "Ferrari looks to be very strong. They have some nice upgrades, and Red Bull. It looks to me like Ferrari might be the team to beat this weekend," said McLaren boss Zak Brown. Leclerc would have been top, had he not had his best lap deleted for exceeding track limits at Turn Nine, while Hamilton also had to take evasive action on a late fast lap to avoid Gabriel Bortoleto's slow Audi ahead of him. Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who can take the title on Sunday if he wins and other results go his way, was fifth fastest -- also losing a lap time due to track limits -- with closest rival and teammate George Russell fourth. Antonelli leads Russell by 102 points with five races remaining after Austin, unless the last two in the Middle East have to be cancelled due to conflict in the region. Four-time world champion Verstappen has won the last two races in Malaysia and Singapore and was also the winner from pole in Austin last season. McLaren's Oscar Piastri was sixth fastest, with teammate and reigning champion Lando Norris eighth. Audi's Nico Hulkenberg was sandwiched between the pair in seventh. Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Red Bull's Isack Hadjar completed the top 10 on the timesheets.

item.title: Burnley dismiss coach Hayen after 14 games
item.description: Burnley have parted ways with head coach Nicky Hayen after just 14 matches, the Championship club said on Saturday, following a poor start to the season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Burnley have parted ways with head coach Nicky Hayen after just 14 matches, the Championship club said on Saturday, following a poor start to the season. The 46-year-old Belgian's final game in charge was Saturday's 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City, a result that extended Burnley's struggles and left them 22nd in the table. Burnley have won only once in their last 12 league matches. "Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season," the club said in a statement. Hayen was appointed on a [USN:L6N43C0YF TEXT:"three-year deal in the summer"], replacing Scott Parker, who left by mutual consent in April after Burnley's relegation from the Premier League was confirmed, with the club dropping into the Championship for the third time in five seasons Hayen was named caretaker manager of Club Brugge in March 2024. He guided the team to the 2023-24 Belgian Pro League title and the Champions League last 16 the following season. After being appointed on a permanent basis in June 2024, he also won the Belgian Cup and Belgian Super Cup and was named Belgium's Coach of the Year in 2024.

item.title: Lazio go top with win over Parma as Roma rally to draw 3-3 at Napoli
item.description: Lazio climbed to the top of the Serie A table with a 2-1 home win over Parma on Saturday as AS Roma twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating Serie A clash in Naples.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lazio climbed to the top of the Serie A table with a 2-1 home win over Parma on Saturday as AS Roma twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating Serie A clash in Naples. Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor netted his first goal of the season, before Parma's Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying to cut out a cross. The visitors scored a late consolation through Simone Lontani. Third-placed Roma trailed 2-0 and then 3-2 late on, so will be pleased with a point in Naples as they preserved their 15-game unbeaten run in Serie A that dates back to April. Frank Anguissa’s spectacular overhead kick gave Napoli the lead and Scott McTominay doubled the advantage. At that stage they were cruising, but two goals in four minutes from Matias Soule and Leonardo Balerdi drew Roma level. When McTominay added his second in the closing stages the momentum swung back in Napoli’s favour, but Balerdi headed an equaliser for Roma with a minute remaining. "We maintained roles, positions and our way of playing," Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini told DAZN. "The goals were of quality. We are fine (with the result), with high morale. "Balerdi knows football, has extraordinary energy and has been a great (loan) signing for us." DOUVIKAS DOUBLE Two second-half goals from Anastasios Douvikas took Como to a 2-0 victory against Sassuolo as the Greek striker continued his red-hot form. He has scored five goals in his last four games in all competitions and provided two clinical finishes in the box as Como climbed to fourth place with 17 points from their eight games. Sassuolo are in 14th. "He (Douvikas) is growing in a way that could make him a very, very important centre-forward," Como coach Cesc Fabregas said. "In the last three years he has been one of those signings that has given a lot of satisfaction." Bologna were 2-0 winners at Cagliari as they claimed their second victory of the season. Defender Nicolo Casale scored his first goal in almost four years to give Bologna the lead before Federico Bernardeschi doubled the advantage for the visitors. "It was a very difficult game on a tough pitch," Bernardeschi said. "These games are won with character. Cagliari made us suffer, but in the second half we reacted well."

item.title: Blackhawks, Panthers look to correct mistakes ahead of Sunday matinee
item.description: Start strong, finish feebly.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Start strong, finish feebly. The Chicago Blackhawks have followed that pattern more often than they'd prefer over the first 10 games of the season. A Sunday matinee against the visiting Florida Panthers offers the next chance for Chicago to correct. "I still like our team a lot," Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill said. "We haven't had a full group yet. I look forward to that day when we have our full group. We're 3-7, so that's way far off from where we want to be. I don't think we're far off from it clicking and turning the other way, but we got to make it happen. ... It'll be a broken record until we fix it." Chicago fell to 2-3-0 on a seven-game homestand with Friday's 4-1 loss to the Montreal Canadiens. Skating without defenseman Bowen Byram (upper body) and forward Andrew Mangiapane, who earlier in the day was activated from injured reserve, the Blackhawks still built early momentum. Captain Connor Bedard scored 4:23 into the game and Jordan Greenway hit the post later in the first period. But the Blackhawks conceded a goal at 17:29 to begin a string of four straight Montreal tallies to close the game. In the third, the Blackhawks needed 8:45 to register their first shot on goal. "We need to have some conversations ... and figure out how we can be better, because clearly (what we're doing is) not good enough," defenseman Ian Cole said. "We start the game well, come out looking good, flying, speeding fast -- that's great, but ultimately they take it to us." Meanwhile, slumping Florida has allowed nine successive goals since Brady Tkachuk scored midway through the first period of Wednesday's visit to Ottawa, where Tkachuk played for eight seasons. The Senators rallied for a 5-1 victory, then the host Pittsburgh Penguins prevailed 4-0 over the Panthers on Thursday. Sam Reinhart had six shots and Sam Bennett four but the Panthers couldn't solve Penguins goaltender Arturs Silovs as Florida was shut out for the first time this season. "I don't know if we're on the spectrum of arrogance and softness that I've allowed to creep into our game," Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. "I'm going to find that out here in a couple of days. ... I've got to figure out where it's coming from. I think it's coming from me. So, we've got a good 48 hours to grind on that and come up with an answer. "I just need to get their attention." Added Matthew Tkachuk: "This stuff just can't happen. It's not even how we're losing, it's the way we're playing. It's something that we're going to have to fix in here." Although the lopsided losses have felt repetitive, the Panthers nonetheless were part of league history Thursday behind goaltender Cooper Black. The 6-foot-9 rookie became the tallest netminder to appear in the NHL, making 17 saves. Defenseman Gustav Forsling left the game late in the third period after being hit in the face by a puck. Akira Schmid is set to start in net, Maurice said Saturday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump administration demands county election officials identify noncitizen voters in California
item.description: Less than two weeks before US midterm elections, the Department of Justice has warned election officials across California they could be targets of federal "scrutiny" if they refuse to help identify suspected noncitizens on voter rolls and set aside their mail ballots pending citizenship checks.
item.dc:creator: David Brunnstrom
item.content:encoded: Less than two weeks before US midterm elections, the Department of Justice has warned election officials across California they could be targets of federal "scrutiny" if they refuse to help identify suspected noncitizens on voter rolls and set aside their mail ballots pending citizenship checks. According to letters dated Friday, local officials were given 48 hours to help determine the citizenship status of individuals on federal government lists. The Justice Department shared with Reuters texts of six of the letters on Saturday, which were signed by Bilal Essayli, first assistant US attorney for the Central District of California. He warned counties that continuing to process ballots from individuals on the list without verifying citizenship status risked "significant federal scrutiny and legal exposure." Officials who knowingly counted ballots cast by individuals identified by federal agencies as noncitizens risked becoming "aiders and abettors to a federal crime," Essayli wrote. Each letter includes local statistics drawn from a previously distributed list of 20,000 people who the Justice Department alleges are noncitizens registered to vote. For those whose "citizenship status cannot be confirmed, we request that you immediately instruct the appropriate elections official to segregate — not cancel — those individuals' vote-by-mail ballots until their citizenship status can be determined," Essayli wrote. The Justice Department said it identified 1,754 suspected noncitizens registered to vote in Orange County, 1,355 in Riverside County, 1,133 in San Bernardino County, 334 in Ventura County, 180 in Santa Barbara County and 63 in San Luis Obispo County. Another letter separately shared by Contra Costa County listed "407 likely aliens" registered. "This letter came to us 11 days before Election Day with an unenforceable 48-hour deadline," said Dawn Kruger, a spokesperson for Contra Costa County’s Elections Department, adding: "Our office is conducting this election in accordance with federal and state laws and that is what we will continue to do." Versions of the letters were sent to all 58 California counties, according to the New York Times. In the run-up to the midterms, the Justice Department has ramped up prosecutions of people accused of illegally voting while not holding US citizenship. The White House has also pushed federal agencies to accelerate their review of at least 47 state voter rolls obtained by the Department of Homeland Security, according to an internal email seen by Reuters. On October 16, the Justice Department warned Los Angeles County and California election officials they could be liable as [USN:L1N46212B TEXT:"abettors of a federal crime"] if they count mail ballots returned by more than 20,000 people the Trump administration says are probably noncitizens. California officials have rejected the moves, saying the federal government has not provided sufficient information about how it identified the alleged noncitizens. California Secretary of State Shirley Weber has accused the administration of attempting to unlawfully access protected voter data and purge voter rolls, saying such efforts undermine confidence in elections.

item.title: Protests sweep Italian cities amid heavy security presence, some violence reported
item.description: Protests against war and rising living costs took place in major Italian cities on Saturday, with some incidents of violence, a week after unrest erupted across the country.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Protests against war and rising living costs took place in major Italian cities on Saturday, with some incidents of violence, a week after unrest erupted across the country. Authorities deployed a heavy police presence and many shops closed as a precaution against possible damage. The demonstrations, [USN:L8N4650S6 TEXT:"which followed clashes last weekend"] in which protesters fought with police, looted shops and vandalised property, were violent in Turin, Rome and Bologna, with clashes between officers and demonstrators. They were largely peaceful in Milan. Reuters witnesses did not observe any shops being looted or property vandalised. After calls for further demonstrations circulated on social media this week, authorities made extensive security arrangements and deployed large numbers of police officers to prevent a repeat of last weekend's violence. Earlier on Saturday, Italian police said they had detained a person allegedly linked to organising the "October 17 Movement" — last weekend's protests — and had taken them to police headquarters in Milan for questioning.

item.title: Merz hace un llamamiento a la unidad, advierte de las amenazas a las que se enfrenta Alemania
item.description: El canciller Friedrich Merz hizo un llamamiento el sábado a la unidad en su coalición, y afirmó que Alemania se enfrentaba a amenazas crecientes por parte de extremistas políticos y a lo que describió como esfuerzos diarios de Rusia por desestabilizar el país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El canciller Friedrich Merz hizo un llamamiento el sábado a la unidad en su coalición, y afirmó que Alemania se enfrentaba a amenazas crecientes por parte de extremistas políticos y a lo que describió como esfuerzos diarios de Rusia por desestabilizar el país. En su intervención en una conferencia de la Unión Social Cristiana (CSU), el partido hermano bávaro de su partido conservador, la Unión Demócrata Cristiana (CDU), Merz afirmó que Alemania se enfrenta a "retos extraordinariamente graves". "¿Cómo salvaguardamos nuestra libertad y nuestra seguridad en Europa, ante las crecientes amenazas de los extremistas internos y de las potencias extranjeras?", preguntó, y añadió que Rusia trata de "desestabilizar a Alemania a diario". Las relaciones entre Berlín y Moscú han caído a su nivel más bajo desde la Guerra Fría tras la invasión rusa de Ucrania en 2022, pero Moscú rechaza las acusaciones de que esté llevando a cabo una campaña híbrida contra Alemania y otros países europeos. Las declaraciones de Merz se producen tras semanas de tensión con la coalición gobernante, a raíz de las contundentes derrotas en las elecciones regionales del este de Alemania, donde el partido de extrema derecha Alternativa para Alemania (AfD) quedó en primer lugar en dos estados y el Partido de Izquierda, de extrema izquierda, se impuso en Berlín. Los índices de popularidad de Merz han caído a mínimos históricos, mientras que han surgido tensiones tanto entre los socios de la coalición como entre la CDU y la CSU.

item.title: 76ers' LeBron James (back management) out vs. visiting Bucks
item.description: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James has been ruled out of Saturday's game against the visiting Milwaukee Bucks because of lower back management.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James has been ruled out of Saturday's game against the visiting Milwaukee Bucks because of lower back management. The 41-year-old has been managing sciatica since the start of the 2025-26 season and will have the night off, according to the NBA's official injury report. James is averaging 33.5 minutes, 15.5 points, 9.5 rebounds and 6.0 assists through two games with his new team. The 2-0 76ers defeated the defending champion New York Knicks 106-100 on Tuesday before erasing a 29-point deficit against the Cleveland Cavaliers for a 114-106 victory Thursday.
