item.title: Jordan church attack survivor says assailant pointed handgun at him
item.description: Prayer services had just started at a church in Jordan on Friday when Nasser al-Burqan heard what he thought was an exploding air conditioner. Then the blasts kept coming. He soon realised it was gunfire.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
item.content:encoded: Prayer services had just started at a church in Jordan on Friday when Nasser al-Burqan heard what he thought was an exploding air conditioner. Then the blasts kept coming. He soon realised it was gunfire. Some people ran away. He said others, some bleeding, tried to hide in their place of worship where a funeral for his relative had been taking place. Word spread among those gathered that there were fatalities. When the shooting finally stopped after several minutes, Burqan said he got a good look at the assailants behind what Jordanian authorities described as an act of extremist terrorism that [USN:L1N46A01M TEXT:"killed eight people"]. “When everything finally quietened down, I looked out the window behind me and I saw two — one was masked, the other was not, he was carrying a handgun,” said Burqan, a lawyer. He said one of the attackers, standing about 2 meters away, pointed the handgun at him and opened fire. Some shattered glass left blood on his face. He said he told people who wanted to take him for medical treatment he was fine. SON SHOT IN THE LEG A short while later his son, who also attended the mass, called him to say he had been shot in the leg and was being treated in hospital. The attack at the Greek Orthodox Hamoud church in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman, shocked the community, part of Jordan’s Christian minority. Such attacks are rare in Jordan, although authorities in the US-allied kingdom say they have repeatedly foiled plots by Islamist militants in recent years. Jordan's King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against militant Islamist groups, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist". Authorities have said they are still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. There has been no immediate claim of responsibility. Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan, the US embassy in Amman said on Saturday, as authorities searched for the gunmen who also wounded 40 people.

item.title: With his first smartphone, Lula seeks to catch up to Brazil's online generation
item.description: "I’m becoming the king of selfies, a real internet user," Lula told supporters.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Novaes Magalhaes, Oliver Griffin, Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: Just days before his 81st birthday, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva this week took ownership of a brand new smartphone, one that former aides said was his first ever. Lula's choice to finally adopt a foundational artefact of modern life may be a tacit acknowledgment that he has failed to keep pace with a Brazilian electorate that now spends much of its life [USN:L1N45Z0NR TEXT:"online"]. That may count against him in Sunday's [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"presidential runoff"]. "I’m becoming the king of selfies, a real internet user," Lula told supporters at a recent rally in Brasilia, hinting at his renewed efforts to better navigate social media campaigning. Lula’s new technological adventure illustrates a generational shift in Brazilian politics, where a candidate's ability to convert millions of followers across platforms like TikTok, Instagram and WhatsApp into votes can now catapult them to the upper echelons of Brazilian power. During [USN:L1N45L166 TEXT:"congressional elections"] that took place alongside the first round of this month's presidential vote, a number of younger, social media-savvy candidates dominated their races. Running for the right-wing Liberal Party, Nikolas Ferreira, 30, and Lucas Pavanato, 28, both took more than 3 million votes in their respective races, while leftist candidates who were elected with over half a million votes each included Erika Hilton, 33, and Ana Elisa Silva, who is just 21. LULA LEARNS THE ROPES Lula, a former shoeshine boy turned metal worker, trade union leader and global leftist icon, first ran for president in 1989, and is seeking an unprecedented fourth term in office. Standing in his way is right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who is the [USN:L1N466029 TEXT:"son of ex-President Jair Bolsonaro"] and surprised pollsters by topping the first-round vote. The 45-year-old senator has been engaging voters directly with his own YouTube channel. Ana Elisa Silva, a law student from Minas Gerais, joined Lula's inner circle to help him better navigate the unfamiliar social media landscape after his disappointing first-round performance. "In my view, digital communication is not a generational privilege," Silva told Reuters. "Age may influence familiarity with certain platforms and formats, but it does not determine the ability to communicate, mobilize, or build a community." For a politician like Lula — who freely admits his distaste for cellphones — the change required some adjustments, Silva said. "His political communication trajectory predates the internet. (It was) forged through his relationships with workers, trade unions, grassroots movements, and massive rallies," she said. "This experience remains important, but it needs to align with changes in how people consume information, especially young people." THE EVOLUTION OF POLITICS The emerging power of so-called "influencer politicians" represents the natural evolution of a phenomenon that started with politicians reaching out to social media figures for campaign support, said Maximo Zaldivar, regional director for Latin America and the Caribbean at the International Foundation for Electoral Systems. "The influencer has their own political capital," Zaldivar said, referring to their amassed followings across social media platforms. "That's what they bring to the table and no politician can compete with that." Among "influencer politicians," Ferreira sits in a league of his own. A staunch Bolsonaro supporter and the son of an evangelical pastor, he boasts nearly 25 million followers on Instagram, equivalent to more than 10% of Brazil's population. Though anyone can jump on social media, success demands commitment and consistent messaging, said Julia Zanatta, 41, an influential conservative lawmaker from southern Brazil with over 1 million followers on Instagram. She secured more than half a million votes in this month's election. “I never thought about whether I'd reach more people or if I'd displease anyone,” she said.

item.title: Divided over Israel, Detroit Democrats unite on rising costs for midterm elections
item.description: It was her son’s eighth birthday, but Dayna Broadnax could not afford a present.
item.dc:creator: Heather Schlitz
item.content:encoded: It was her son’s eighth birthday, but Dayna Broadnax could not afford a present. Broadnax, a 42-year-old single mother of four in Detroit, said soaring gas and grocery prices left little money to pay the bills, let alone buy gifts or throw a birthday party. “It’s hard to tell your kids that you don't have the funds right now to buy them a $3 bag of Skittles,” she said while watching her sons practice with a free basketball team at St. Suzanne Community Resource Center. Ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, Broadnax’s concerns are widely shared in Detroit. Jewish, Muslim and Black voters interviewed by Reuters often put affordability ahead of disputes over Israel and Gaza, even as many expressed reservations about Democratic US Senate nominee [USN:L1N4420RK TEXT:"Abdul El-Sayed"]. El-Sayed, who could make history as the first Muslim US senator, faces former congressman Mike Rogers in a competitive race that could help determine control of the Senate. A RealClearPolitics average gives El-Sayed a two-point lead – 48% to 46%. Broadnax has yet to decide who to support, saying she will vote for the candidate most focused on lowering costs. She sometimes skips meals so her children can eat and chooses which bills to pay after gas eats up at least $50 of the $150 she makes on a typical day driving for Lyft. “Being a single mom, trying to take care of four boys out here in America now is too hard,” she said. “Whatever candidate whose main focus is affordability – that’s who I’m going with.” But El-Sayed faces resistance from some voters who would ordinarily be inclined to support a Democrat, particularly over Israel. “Both of the candidates have decided that this election is about Abdul,” said Matt Grossmann, a political science professor at Michigan State University. “He needs to win over voters that would normally support the Democratic candidate and are upset with President Trump but might have reservations about him – personal or policy reservations.” El-Sayed’s challenge is not only keeping uneasy Democrats from voting for Rogers, but getting them to vote at all. Some voters told Reuters that opposing Trump made backing Rogers difficult, while concerns about El-Sayed led others to consider sitting out the race. JEWISH VOTERS’ RESERVATIONS Most Jewish voters in Detroit traditionally vote Democratic, but some have deep reservations about El-Sayed over his views on Israel, particularly his response to a March attack on a suburban synagogue. After a man rammed his truck into Temple Israel while more than 100 children were inside, El-Sayed drew backlash when he said “hurt people hurt people" in reference to the attacker. Though El-Sayed later apologized for the comment, he has continued to draw heavy criticism from a community shaken by the attack. Rabbi Aaron Starr of Congregation Shaarey Zedek said some Jewish men now cover their heads with baseball caps instead of yarmulkes because they fear being targeted if identified as Jews. Starr's synagogue spends twice as much on security measures for its sprawling campus following the attack. Starr and a group of Jewish clergy launched a petition calling for the Democratic Party to agree to a set of “non-negotiable” principles, including acknowledging Israel’s right to exist and Jewish sovereignty in Israel. El-Sayed has not signed the petition or communicated with the group, Starr said. He said he would not vote for the Democratic nominee. “He is hyper-focused on Israel and American supporters of the state of Israel and seemed to be placing an awful lot of blame on Israel for America's problems,” Starr said in his study, where “hurt people help people” yard signs leaned against a wall beside shelves of religious texts. El-Sayed briefly campaigned with Hasan Piker, a left-wing streamer who has drawn criticism over comments about Israel and American Jews. The association has troubled some voters, while others remain more focused on the cost of living. “I don't love the fact that he campaigned with Hasan Piker during the primary,” said Alicia Chandler, a 47-year-old Jewish Detroit resident and former supporter of El-Sayed's Democratic primary opponent Haley Stevens. “But it cost me almost $100 to fill my car with gas yesterday.” El-Sayed has repeatedly pledged to protect Jewish people from antisemitism, saying in an August speech after winning the Democratic primary that his commitment to Jewish safety was “the same commitment that I have to the safety of my own daughters.” GAZA AND THE POCKETBOOK In 2024, frustration with the Biden-Harris administration’s support for Israel’s war in Gaza drove many Arab American and Muslim voters in Michigan away from the Democratic ticket, with some backing the Republican Trump or third-party candidates and others choosing not to vote. At Shibam Coffee, a Yemeni coffeehouse in the Arab-majority city of Dearborn, volunteers wearing “Abdul for Senate” shirts gathered over cardamom coffee, honeycomb bread and sambusas before heading out to canvass. The cafe is popular with young Arab Americans, many of whom now support El-Sayed. Sumayah Dhalai, a 22-year-old senior at Wayne State University who plans to vote for El-Sayed, liked his policy position opposing funding for the Israeli government but said her fears about finding a job and affording rent and groceries were a bigger factor in deciding who to vote for. “The overwhelming majority of us are very scared about graduating because everybody’s telling us that everything sucks,” Dhalai said. “As much as I want to say I'm out here fighting for world peace, I have to ensure my own ability to succeed before I can then turn to focus on everybody else's.” While parts of Detroit have benefited from new investment, others have not, including the neighborhood housing St. Suzanne Community Resource Center, where the median household income is just $36,525 and roughly half the children live in poverty, according to US Census data. “The financial stress is continual,” said Steve Wasko, the director of the center where Broadnax's sons play basketball. “Being able to pay your rent, afford your light bill, pay your mortgage, or pay to have your furnace working sufficiently – these are the most common requests that come through the door."

item.title: Five takeaways from Trump's midterm campaign rallies
item.description: Trump has long had a fixation on the human physique that stretches beyond the body politic.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Bo Erickson, Nandita Bose, Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump is in the midst of a nationwide campaign blitz ahead of the November midterm elections, holding near-daily rallies to boost turnout for Republicans who are fighting to keep control of Congress. In his 90-minute stump speeches, Trump defends his economic policies, boasts about crowd size, mocks protesters and has even admired a fellow Republican’s buttocks. Here are five takeaways from Reuters coverage of the president’s appearances, staged mostly in Republican-friendly areas across the country: TRUMP'S ECONOMIC PITCH COLLIDES WITH VOTER REALITY At the start of the month, Trump said he had done a “[USN:L1N45M10K TEXT:"bad job"]” explaining his economic record. He has tried to remedy that at his rallies, pointing to a record-low [USN:S0N4310A5 TEXT:"poverty rate"], low [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"unemployment,"] record highs in the [USN:L6N45S0IV TEXT:"stock market"] and cheaper prices for some food items. But his sales pitch is colliding with voters' concerns about how much they are spending on gas, groceries and other everyday expenses. Consumer prices accelerated in September as the cost of gasoline surged. The nationwide average price of gas is $4.27 per gallon ($1.13 per litre), nearly 40% higher than a year ago, according to AAA. Trump has repeatedly promised that gas prices will fall once the Iran war ends. The disconnect was evident outside Trump's rally in rural Kansas, where Chester Daniel, a 90-year-old military veteran and Trump supporter, said the economy has “a long way to go” to help working people. “Prices? Too high! We will never go back to what they were when this all started, but they need to come way down," Daniel said. "I don’t know how these young people make a living for their family." RALLY MAP SHOWS REPUBLICANS PLAYING DEFENSE Trump's travel map signals just how difficult it will be for Republicans to retain control of Congress, with the president forced to play defense deep in conservative territory. Trump has traveled twice to Texas for Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton, campaigned for Republican Senate incumbent Roger Marshall in Kansas and made two stops in Ohio for Senator Jon Husted. Trump also rallied for Republicans in competitive races in Alaska, Iowa, Montana and South Carolina. He is set to visit Mississippi on Monday. Those are places Republicans are accustomed to winning easily, not battlegrounds where Trump would spend time during the crucial final weeks before an election. Paxton narrowly trails Democrat James Talarico in polls, while Marshall faces a serious challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton in a state that has not elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century. Husted trails former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown in polls in Ohio, and Republican Senate hopeful Ashley Hinson is in a close race against Democrat Josh Turek in Iowa. Notably absent from Trump's travels so far with less than two weeks until Election Day: Michigan, Maine, Minnesota and New Hampshire – also home to tight Senate races. He is soon poised to hit some of those locations. He is scheduled travel to Michigan on Sunday and has said he also plans to go to Maine. TRUMP'S BOASTS ABOUT BIG CROWDS MEET UNEVEN REALITY Trump has made crowd sizes a recurring theme of his midterm rallies, portraying packed arenas and thousands of people he says are stranded outside as evidence of his persisting popularity. But actual turnout on the campaign trail in recent weeks has been uneven. Some rallies have drawn capacity crowds but have shown little sign of the overflow Trump described. At others, large sections of seats remained empty even in modest-sized venues. "I'm doing these every night, and no matter where I go, it's the same thing. It's massive crowds," Trump said at a rally in North Carolina on Tuesday. "We have big screens outside. Thousands and thousands of people. There's something going on that's very special." The venue was filled to capacity, but there were no signs of crowds outside waiting to get in or watching on screens. At an October 7 rally in San Antonio, Texas, Trump said lines stretched two miles outside the arena even as sizable sections inside remained empty. Crowd sizes are not always an accurate measure of political support, but Trump has pointed to them as a sign of strength even as his approval rating has fallen to 31%, the lowest of either of his presidential terms, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll released on Monday. Trump is not on the ballot on November 3. For Republican candidates, the question is whether the enthusiasm he generates among his supporters can translate into votes for them. FRANCE BECOMES A 'BETE NOIRE' FOR MIDTERMS Trump has often used French President Emmanuel Macron as a foil in his campaign stump speeches, claiming he strong-armed Macron into raising prescription drug prices in France by threatening tariffs on a popular French export, champagne, and other goods. But in the last week or so Trump has seized on another narrative about France, casting its violent unrest of recent weeks as a warning of what he says could happen in the US if Democrats win in the midterms. Trump has blamed the unrest on migrants and Muslims, following a familiar playbook that has featured in his politics for more than a decade. “What the hell happened to France?” Trump told a crowd in a livestock competition arena in Clemson, South Carolina, on Wednesday. Notably, the French protests have taken a larger role in Trump’s recent speeches than two other major foreign policy headaches he has been unable to resolve: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and his war against Iran. “They’ll end one way or another,” Trump said of the two conflicts at his Clemson rally. He did not elaborate on how they might end, but complained that he was not awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his work to resolve conflicts around the world. TRUMP PUTS THE BODY IN BODY POLITIC Trump has long had a fixation on the human physique that stretches beyond the body politic. This campaign season, Trump has given particular attention to Husted, a 59-year-old former college football player for the University of Dayton. At rallies in Ohio, Kentucky and North Carolina, Trump marveled at Husted’s physique, at one point saying his backside is “like a pile of muscle.” “Then I looked at his legs, and I said, ‘Man, his feet are big.’ Then I looked at his shoulders, and I tapped him on the shoulder, and it actually hurt my hand. It was like a piece of steel. I said, ‘This guy’s a monster,’” Trump said. Trump had similar praise on Friday for Robert F. Kennedy Jr., his secretary of health and human services, telling a campaign rally in Florida that the 72-year-old "has the body of a 30-year-old." Such riffs are familiar terrain for Trump. At the close of his 2024 campaign, he used a Pennsylvania rally speech to tell a crude story about PGA legend Arnold Palmer's prowess beyond his golf game. Trump's focus over the years on people's physical attributes has also included mocking the weight and looks of his opponents. Trump finds even some of his friends lacking in fashion sense, including the rumpled Paxton. "Some may not like the way he dresses," Trump said about him at the Republicans' midterm convention in Dallas in mid-September, adding: "I don't." That has not stopped Trump from campaigning for Paxton, however. He returns to Texas on Tuesday for two more campaign rallies.

item.title: Violence flares in Paris after largely peaceful protests across France
item.description: The interior minister mobilized 70,000 police nationwide, 10,000 more than on October 17, when vandalism and looting raised questions about the government's ability to maintain order.
item.dc:creator: Juliette Jabkhiro, Yann Tessier, Crispian Balmer
item.content:encoded: Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators marched in France on Saturday, with largely peaceful rallies giving way to clashes in Paris and Marseille as night fell despite a huge security operation aimed at preventing a repeat of [USN:L1N46608H TEXT:"last week's unrest"]. The Interior Ministry said 410,000 people took part in protests nationwide, though unions said the true figure was twice as high. The main demonstration took place on the southeastern fringes of Paris, where at least 110,000 people turned out to denounce rising living costs and growing inequality. The atmosphere deteriorated sharply after the rally ended. Riot police fired tear gas and water cannon at a group of around 500 hooded youths before they eventually dispersed on a cold, rainy evening. In France's second city, Marseille, youths set fire to rubbish bins to block roads, and hurled rocks and bottles at security forces. Police said several stores, including two jewellery shops, were ransacked. Clashes also flared in Lyon, Bordeaux, Grenoble, Clermont-Ferrand, Lille, Rennes, Nantes and Toulouse. "In almost every march we saw the formation of these high-risk groups. They broke away from the main body and sought to commit acts of violence," said Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, accusing far-left activists and criminal gangs of seeking to foment trouble. PARIS IN LOCKDOWN Authorities deployed 70,000 police officers and gendarmes, 10,000 more than a week earlier, after conceding they had underestimated the scale of the unrest on October 17. Nunez told reporters the violence was less intense than a week ago, when looters and vandals went on the rampage. "What changed was anticipation," he said. He also said far-right activists had sought confrontations with leftist groups in the southern cities of Nice and Montpellier, opening a potential new front in the disturbances. Much of central Paris took on the appearance of a city under lockdown, with shopkeepers [USN:L2N46A00I TEXT:"boarding up storefronts"], [USN:L5N46A022 TEXT:"museums closing their doors"] and more than 20 metro stations shut. Business groups urged retailers to remain closed after thousands of shops and businesses were damaged or looted across France last weekend. "There are hardly any customers, so it's not really worth staying open," said Oskar, manager of a Kiton boutique in Paris. Several of the capital's best-known cultural institutions, including the Louvre, the Musee d'Orsay and the Paris Opera, closed for the day as a precaution, leaving tourists frustrated. "Everything's boarded up and we're not quite sure where we should be," said Xavier Dolliole, a tourist from the US city of New Orleans. PROTESTS RIPPLE ACROSS EUROPE The nationwide disorder began with small student demonstrations in suburban Paris last month to denounce school conditions. It swiftly broadened into a wider protest against the government's economic policies and inspired demonstrations in neighbouring countries. On Saturday [USN:L6N46A05C TEXT:"Belgian police"] used tear gas and pepper spray as they clashed in Brussels with anti-government demonstrators, with protests also taking place in a number of Italian cities for a second weekend, [USN:L2N46A02Y TEXT:"and in Albania"]. Hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon, who joined the Paris rally, predicted the protests would continue until President Emmanuel Macron, whose mandate expires next year, addressed the social malaise in France, one of the world's richest nations. "Given the current situation, I think he will come to understand that this will happen again every week. There is still time for (Macron) to give in. After that, the only thing left to him will be the exit door," Melenchon told reporters. FAR-RIGHT PARTY HOLDS CONGRESS Many demonstrators accused the government of overreacting to last week's turmoil, as soldiers were dispatched to patrol the Champs-Elysees, a grand boulevard lined with luxury shops and restaurants. "We shed tears for shops, not for the people who are being impoverished all year round," said Clara Lebbadi, a 22-year-old arts student. "My friend and I almost didn't come because we were scared, but we came precisely because it's important not to let repression win," she added. The first authorised march on Saturday passed off peacefully in Orléans, around 120 km (75 miles) south of Paris, where demonstrators rallied against Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally, which is holding a party congress in the city. A [USN:L6N4690NC TEXT:"shooting"] west of Paris on Friday heightened tensions. A gunman suspected of acting out of Islamophobic hatred killed one person and wounded four others, including a 12-year-old girl. "We have come to tell the far right, face-to-face, that we are not afraid," said Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of Saint-Denis and a member of Melenchon's France Unbowed party.

item.content:encoded:

Ukraine says Starlink and Starshield operating at 400 kph after week of throttling

Reuters

24 October, 2026 03:00 pm IST

Facebook

Follow Us :

KYIV, Oct 24 (Reuters) – The Starlink satellite communications system and its military version Starshield are operating again at speeds over 400 km per hour, Kyiv’s defence minister said on Saturday, after over a week of service restrictions that slowed connections and disrupted military operations.

“The Ministry of Defence’s monitoring systems are recording a return to normal speed for Starlink/Starshield. We are recording a speed of over 400 kph. The connection is stable,” Evhenii Khmara told reporters.

The Ukrainian military does not disclose the systems’ maximum operating speeds, and the defence ministry did not say whether service had been fully restored.

Show Full Article

“Monitoring systems had previously recorded disruptions to the Starlink/Starshield service. The speed metrics have now returned to normal,” the ministry said.

The restrictions, first reported on October 14, undermined Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian attack drones and disrupted frontline communications, Ukrainian officials said. Sources said connection speeds had been reduced to about 160 kph or less.

Ukraine’s problems with SpaceX-owned Starlink came after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and waived new sanctions on Moscow while pressing Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries.

Neither SpaceX boss Elon Musk nor the US government has acknowledged responsibility for restricting Starlink or Starshield in Ukraine. Both have said publicly that any such decision could only have been taken by the other.

Reuters has reported that the order to throttle Starshield came from inside the White House.

Trump said on Friday that if problems with access to Starlink communications systems in Ukraine persisted, he would “get it straightened out”.

(Reporting by Dan Peleschuk, writing by Yuliia DysaEditing by Ros Russell)

item.title: Ukraine says Starshield back to normal, Musk says Kyiv violated terms
item.description: A week of restrictions disrupted military operations and intensified tensions with the US.
item.dc:creator: Yuliia Dysa
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said on Saturday that the Starlink satellite system and its military version Starshield were now fully functional after over a week of restrictions that disrupted military operations and intensified tensions with the US. But hours later, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, whose company owns Starlink, accused the Ukrainian military of violating the company's terms. Neither Musk nor the US government, which operates Starshield using Starlink technology, had taken responsibility for imposing the curbs. "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week," Musk said on X. Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said on the Telegram app that the country is "physically unable" to use Starlink for long- and medium-range attack drone operations. Ukraine's general staff and defence ministry did not immediately comment. Starshield's problems occurred after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel while pressing Kyiv to stop striking Russian oil refineries. Ukrainian officials said the restrictions, which capped Starshield operations at speeds of 160 kph (100 mph), hampered the military's ability to intercept Russian attack drones and forced the cancellation of some operations. "The main thing for today is that Starlink and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the level we need," President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Telegram before Musk's statement. According to Zelenskiy, the speeds started returning to normal overnight. Ukraine's defence ministry said on Saturday the connection remained stable at over 400 kph. Ukraine does not rely on Starlink for long-range drone operations on Russian territory, including attacks on refineries. It operates at speeds no higher than 70-90 kph, Beskrestnov said. But it remains [USN:L6N4690ON TEXT:"vital"] for frontline communications, and the deployment of fast Starshield-enabled medium-range attack drones has helped Ukraine gain the upper hand in several areas of the battlefield this year. LIMITATIONS ORDER The restrictions sparked outrage in Ukraine, particularly as they coincided with disruptions to allied warnings about incoming Russian missile attacks. Kyiv later said it continued to receive US intelligence. Both Musk and US officials said publicly that any decisions on Starlink and Starshield limitations could only have been taken by the other. Reuters has reported that the [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"order to throttle"] Starshield came from inside the White House. Previously, US administrations had several times [USN:L4N4691IH TEXT:"asked SpaceX"] to turn Starlink on or off in various countries, sources said. On Friday, contradicting his previous statement that the services had been fully restored, Trump said that if problems persisted, he would "[USN:L6N4690ZQ TEXT:"get it straightened out"]".

item.title: Houthis say they targeted Saudi oil sites; attacks reported in Aden
item.description: Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis said they launched attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports on Saturday, and the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it downed two missiles, as clashes between the two sides intensified.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis said they launched attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports on Saturday, and the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it downed two missiles, as clashes between the two sides intensified. On another front of an escalating conflict reignited by the Iran war , Yemen's Saudi-backed government said the Houthis also fired three ballistic missiles at coast guard sites in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden. Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements, though they reported missile debris falling near the site of one of the purported oil targets. It was not immediately clear if any of the reported attacks had hit their targets in the kingdom or had been intercepted. SAUDIS REPORT DEBRIS FROM INTERCEPTED MISSILES Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Rabigh oil refinery, crude oil pumping stations and the East-West Pipeline. He also said the group targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, an airport in Najran and an airbase in Khamis Mushait. The Saudi-led coalition earlier said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired by Houthis towards Yanbu and Taif. Saudi Civil Defense said debris from intercepted missiles had fallen in the Mecca and Medina regions, home to Islam's holiest sites visited by millions of Muslim pilgrims every year. It said parts of the intercepted missiles fell in Wadi al-Mughammas in Mecca, while debris also fell in areas in Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh. It was not clear if that was linked to the Houthis' reported targeting of the Rabigh oil refinery. Shortly after that, Houthis denied that they attacked Mecca and Medina, saying that their operations "target Saudi oil facilities and military bases." The renewed fighting has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce that largely halted cross-border attacks between the Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa. The escalation has opened another front in the US-Israeli war on Iran . In Yemen, the Interior Ministry of the internationally recognised government said two of the Houthis' missiles had struck a coast guard headquarters, while a third hit a coast guard building in the Tawahi district. Houthi spokesman Saree said the group's forces had targeted Saudi-backed military gatherings at what he called Al-Nasr camp and a naval base in Aden, saying Saudi officers were overseeing the mobilisation there. There was no immediate comment from the Saudi-led coalition on that assertion. Earlier on Saturday, Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense briefly issued alerts warning residents of potential danger in Taif and Yanbu, as well as in the holy city of Mecca and the kingdom's second-largest city, Jeddah. About 10 minutes later, the agency said the threat had passed. The Houthis warned airlines earlier this month against using Saudi airspace, exempting only the airspace over Mecca and Medina, as they intensified attacks on the kingdom.

item.title: France deploys 70,000 security personnel as new protests raise riot fears
item.description: Paris has boarded up shops and shut 3 major museums ahead of Saturday's protests, while a football match has been postponed; President Macron acknowledged planning failures after last weekend's unrest ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Samy Adghirni A new round of protests is set to hit France Saturday, raising fears of a repeat of last weekend’s riots. The French government has vowed to subdue any violence, deploying 70.000 security officials, including elite anti-terror forces, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told reporters Friday. He blamed social media calls for violence on the far left.  Shops in Paris including luxury boutiques boarded up windows and hired more security personnel, and some will remain shut. Three popular museums, the Louvre, Musee d’Orsay and the Picasso Museum will close Saturday. The scheduled football match between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais in Paris was postponed.  “We will be uncompromising with hooligans, looters, and anyone who commits acts of violence — including far-left political groups,” Nunez said, while stressing that the police is “ready” to face rioters. Soldiers will help guard sensitive buildings. Helicopters, water canons and armored vehicles known as Centaurs will also be available. Some cities, including Lyon, banned protests on Saturday and extended curfews.  President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday acknowledged “planning failings and elements of surprise” last weekend, when protests drew more than half a million people and degenerated into vandalism. Rioters attacked public buildings and looted stores across the country. The French leader, who postponed a planned tour across West Africa, blamed ultra-left groups for what he called seditious acts.  Supported by a disparate movement of social media figures, students, unions and left-wing parties, Saturday’s protests are framed as an “Acte II,” or second round, of a movement calling for better public services and government help with the cost of living. Much of the anger is targeted at Macron, who six months before the end of his second term, has never been so unpopular. Polls show the violence has benefited far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner for next year’s election. Adding to tensions, Le Pen is due to convene thousands of supporters in the central city of Orleans on Saturday for her National Rally party congress. Anti-Le Pen opponents are heading there to protest. The unrest has also increased fears about public finances. While France dodged a downgrade at Moody’s Ratings late Friday, it’s struggling to reduce the budget deficit ahead of the 2027 election. A closely watched gauge of bond risk rose to levels last seen during the euro-area debt crisis: The spread between 10-year yields in France and Germany, the region’s safe asset, reached 178 basis points on Thursday, compared with just 85 basis points at the start of September. Private-sector economic activity also shrank this month, with the Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index compiled by S&P Global dropping to 48.4 in October from 51.1 last month. That’s below the 50 threshold separating expansion from contraction. France isn’t the only European country dealing with a popular anger. In Italy, demonstrations by students and other youth are expected in Milan and Rome over the weekend. The government has said will deploy military forces in Milan after protests led to looting and rioting there last weekend.  Protests are also expected in Belgium while Albania is grappling with a second week of violent student-led demonstrations fueled by discontent with Prime Minister Edi Rama’s rule.

item.title: 金総書記1年ぶり訪中、今月開通の国境橋使用 習指導部要人と会談
item.description: ［ソウル／北京 ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ソウル／北京　２４日　ロイター］ - 北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記は２４日、中国遼寧省丹東を訪問した。中国国営新華社が伝えた。金氏の訪中は２０２５年９月以来、約１年ぶり。中国共産党序列４位の王滬寧・人民政治協商会議（政協）主席が金氏を迎え、会談で習近平国家主席のメッセージを伝えた。

金氏は、今月開通したばかりの、中朝を結ぶ新鴨緑江大橋を渡って丹東に到着した。中国国営中央テレビ（ＣＣＴＶ）の映像には、旗を振る人々が並ぶ橋の上を、金氏が北朝鮮側へ歩く様子が映っていた。

今回の訪問は、１９５０─５３年の朝鮮戦争に中国人民義勇軍が参戦した日の前日というタイミングで、新華社によると、金氏は王氏とともに丹東の朝鮮戦争記念施設を訪れた。当地の自動車工場も視察したという。

一連の予定を終えた金氏は北朝鮮に戻った。韓国聯合ニュースは、王氏が新鴨緑江大橋で見送ったと伝えた。

２５年９月の訪中時は、北京で開かれた戦勝８０周年の記念行事に出席し、習近平国家主席と会談した。習氏は今年６月に北朝鮮を公式訪問した。

トランプ米大統領は北朝鮮との対話再開に意欲を示している。１１月には中国・深センでアジア太平洋経済協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議が開催され、トランプ氏も出席する予定だ。

＜中朝経済関係強化＞

中国は、北朝鮮にとって経済・外交面の主要な後ろ盾で、北朝鮮の公式な貿易の大半を占めている。ただ、ロシアが２０２２年にウクライナに侵攻して以降、北朝鮮はロシアとの軍事関係を深めており、中国への依存が弱まったのではないかとの見方が専門家から出ている。今回の訪中は、中朝が経済関係の強化に改めて取り組んでいることを印象付けた。

新鴨緑江大橋は今月１５日に開通した。橋自体は１４年に完成したが、北朝鮮側の準備が整わず、開通が遅れた。

新しい橋は、北朝鮮が開発に必要とする重機や原材料、エネルギー製品の輸送に役立つと期待されている。王氏は金氏との会談で、中国は橋の開通を機に人的交流や経済・貿易協力を拡大する用意があると伝えた。

オランダのライデン大学で朝鮮半島を専門とするクリストファー・グリーン氏は、橋の開通の遅れは中朝関係がいかに機能不全に陥っていたかを示すと指摘した上で、「金氏は新鴨緑江大橋を渡って中国に入ることで、２国間貿易にお墨付きを与えた」と述べた。

中国政府系シンクタンク、遼寧社会科学院で中朝関係を研究する呂超氏は、金氏の訪中は、中朝の経済関係が緊密になり、ハイレベル交流が頻繁に行われている現在の流れに沿ったものだと述べた。「橋の開通で、物流の制約が和らぎ、２国間貿易はさらに増える可能性が高い」と語った。

item.title: Jordan king orders 'iron fist' response to deadly church attack
item.description: Jordan's King Abdullah ordered security forces on Saturday to respond with an "iron fist" as authorities searched for gunmen who opened fire and killed nine people during a church funeral service.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
item.content:encoded: Jordan's King Abdullah ordered security forces on Saturday to respond with an "iron fist" as authorities searched for gunmen who opened fire and killed nine people during a church funeral service. The assailants [USN:L6N46A02E TEXT:"fired for several minutes"] in broad daylight at the church in Karak governorate on Friday, and also wounded 40 people in the rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority. Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across the country, the US embassy in Amman said. 'A SENSE OF PANIC TOOK HOLD' A priest described how he and others ordered people to get to the ground at Saint George's Greek Orthodox church, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital, Amman. "A sense of panic took hold among those present," Theodoros Soueiss told Reuters. "The gunfire was indiscriminate, and you never knew where a bullet might land." King Abdullah condemned the "despicable terrorist act" as he chaired a National Security Council meeting and said there was no room for leniency when it comes to the lives of Jordanians, the royal court said. Such attacks are highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities there say they have foiled several Islamist plots in recent years. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack in the kingdom, a major partner with the US in the fight against militant groups. Officials have said it is too early to determine whether the attackers had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. "A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word," said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated. A relative of Ammarin's was injured in the attack. Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world. Jordan has been among the US allies in the Middle East to be hit by Iranian attacks this year after the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February. Bahjat al-Rushda, mayor of Shihan village in Karak, joined a long list of officials condemning what they called an attack by extremist terrorists. "God willing, this country will remain secure," he said.

item.title: North Korea's Kim crosses new bridge into China as trade ties warm
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, Xinhua reported, crossing a newly opened bridge in a symbolic move seen as highlighting Beijing and Pyongyang's push to expand trade ties.
item.dc:creator: Joyce Lee, Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday, Xinhua reported, crossing a newly opened bridge in a symbolic move seen as highlighting Beijing and Pyongyang's push to expand trade ties. Kim was accompanied during his visit by China's fourth-highest-ranked official Wang Huning, who conveyed greetings from President Xi Jinping, the official Xinhua news agency said. Kim arrived in Dandong via the [USN:L6N46004I TEXT:"New Yalu River Bridge"] connecting North Korea and China , a South Korean government official said on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak publicly. The new bridge is expected to help move heavy equipment, raw materials and energy products that North Korea needs for development. Its official opening this month is the latest sign of warming ties between Beijing and Pyongyang, after two summits between their leaders in the past 13 months. China, which fought alongside North Korea in the 1950-1953 Korean War, remains Pyongyang's main economic and diplomatic backer and accounts for most of its official trade. CHINESE TV SHOWS KIM WALKING ON BRIDGE But North Korea's deepening military ties with Russia since Moscow's 2022 invasion of Ukraine have led analysts to question whether Pyongyang is becoming less reliant on Beijing. Kim's trip nevertheless points to a renewed push by China and North Korea to bolster their economic relationship. South Korea's Yonhap news agency had earlier reported that Kim was expected to return to North Korea after Saturday's visit. Footage from Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed Kim walking on the bridge, lined by people waving flags, towards North Korea. Xinhua said Wang accompanied Kim to a Korean War memorial in Dandong, where the North Korean leader paid tribute to Chinese People's Volunteer Army soldiers who fought alongside North Korea during the three-year conflict. Kim also toured a Dandong [USN:RTV844HDK TEXT:"automobile factory"], it said. NEW YALU RIVER BRIDGE BOOSTS BILATERAL TIES China and North Korea opened the 3 km (2 mile) New Yalu River Bridge, their most significant [USN:L1N46103M TEXT:"land border crossing"], this month after a long delay, aiming to rejuvenate trade and commerce after years of strained ties and pandemic-related disruptions. "Kim has given his imprimatur to bilateral trade by crossing the New Yalu River Bridge to enter China," said Christopher Green, a Korea specialist at Leiden University in the Netherlands, saying the delayed opening had shown how dysfunctional the relationship had become. During a meeting on Saturday, Wang told Kim that China was ready to use the bridge's opening to expand personnel exchanges and economic and trade cooperation, Xinhua said. A visit by Kim now is consistent with the current phase of closer economic ties and more frequent high-level exchanges between China and North Korea, said Lu Chao, an expert in China-North Korea relations at the Liaoning Academy of Social Sciences, a Chinese government think-tank in Shenyang. "The opening of the bridge has resolved a major bottleneck in China-North Korea trade logistics," Lu said. "With the logistics constraint eased, bilateral trade is likely to increase further." TRUMP WAITS FOR KIM TO ENGAGE Kim's last known visit to China was in September 2025, to attend the 80th Victory Day celebrations in Beijing, when he held a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Xi made a [USN:L1N42G106 TEXT:"state visit"] to North Korea in June. US President Donald Trump has been eager to jump-start talks with North Korea, but US and South Korean officials see [USN:L1N4690EW TEXT:"fading chances"] of him meeting Kim this year, Reuters reported on Friday. China hosts a summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum next month in Shenzhen, which Trump is expected to attend.

item.title: 米英首脳が電話会談、北海油田やウクライナ・フォークランド巡り協議
item.description: ［ワシントン ２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ワシントン　２３日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は２３日、バーナム英首相と電話会談し、北海油田の開発について協議したと明らかにした。イランやウクライナの紛争についても「ごく軽く」触れたとしている。

トランプ氏は、中間選挙に向けフロリダ州での遊説に出発する前、ホワイトハウスで記者団に対し「彼らは北海油田を開放しようとしている」と述べた。「私は２年間それを求めてきた。アンディ（・バーナム氏）がそれを実現しつつある」と語った。

トランプ氏は２１日、英国が北海のジャックドー・ガス田の開発を承認したことを称賛した。

英首相府の声明によると、バーナム氏はまた、フォークランド諸島沖の石油探査問題も取り上げた。同諸島は英国の海外領土で広範な自治権を持つが、アルゼンチンが長年にわたり領有権を主張している。

バーナム氏はウクライナを巡り、ロシアに対して自衛するためにウクライナがスターリンクへの全面的なアクセスを確保することの重要性を強調した。また、ロシアのプーチン大統領を交渉の席に着かせようとするトランプ氏の努力を歓迎した。

両首脳は中東についても協議し、バーナム氏はフーシ派の攻撃に直面するサウジアラビアへの英国の支持を改めて表明したという。

item.title: How Trump's energy dominance turned into hubris
item.description: It was the US position as the world's top oil and gas producer that enabled Trump to pursue foreign-policy goals that may turn out to be the costliest of his political career.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: When Donald Trump returned to the White House in 2025, [USN:L1N3Q1127 TEXT:"“energy dominance”"] was the bedrock of his economic and foreign policy plans. But an unpopular war with Iran and soaring household fuel costs have now made energy policy a major liability for the US president heading into next month’s midterm elections . Ironically, it was the US position as the world's top oil and gas producer, perhaps more than anything else, that enabled Trump to pursue foreign policy goals that may turn out to be the costliest of his political career. In the first two years of Trump’s second term, vast US oil and gas resources emboldened Washington abroad, strengthened its hand in trade disputes and underpinned a broader effort to restore US geopolitical dominance. Yet the Iran war exposed the central weakness in that vision: dominating energy production does not mean controlling energy prices. What began as a pursuit of US energy independence evolved into a doctrine of energy dominance. That is now looking like energy hubris. UNLEASHING AMERICAN ENERGY The foundations of Trump’s strategy were laid long before his return to office last year. The development of cost-effective techniques to tap the country's onshore shale basins transformed the US into the world’s largest producer of natural gas in 2009 and petroleum in 2018. By 2022, it was the leading exporter of liquefied natural gas, giving Washington unprecedented influence over global energy markets. US crude production rose from around 5.5 million barrels per day in 2010 to nearly 14 million bpd today, around a fifth of global supplies, while the country also accounts for more than a quarter of global LNG exports. No single nation has ever occupied such a commanding position in the global energy system. Trump sought to turn that advantage into a governing doctrine. On his first day back in office, he declared a national energy emergency and ordered the government to [USN:S0N3NI004 TEXT:"“unleash American energy”"], prioritising oil, gas, coal and nuclear power while sidelining renewables. Within weeks, he made “energy dominance” official US policy, establishing the National Energy Dominance Council and reviving his familiar “drill, baby, drill” slogan as the purported cure for elevated inflation and economic anxiety. In an October 2025 proclamation, Trump summed up the philosophy as “maximum production, maximum prosperity, and maximum power”. ENERGY POLICY IS FOREIGN POLICY This doctrine extended far beyond domestic energy policy. The administration’s national security strategy, published last December, explicitly linked US influence in the Western Hemisphere to energy dominance, drawing on the 19th-century Monroe Doctrine that sought to oppose European political intervention in the region. In a little over a year, the administration wielded US oil and LNG exports in trade negotiations, promoted energy deals as part of efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war , and highlighted Greenland’s resource wealth in a push for greater influence over the [USN:L6N45E05Y TEXT:"Arctic territory"]. The high-water mark for Trump’s energy doctrine arguably came early this year after [USN:L6N3Y407K TEXT:"Washington removed Venezuelan President"] Nicolas Maduro in a swift military operation. The US subsequently [USN:L1N3ZM1KL TEXT:"took control"] of Venezuelan oil exports and revenues, forced through changes to the country’s hydrocarbons legislation that displaced Chinese companies, and secured an unprecedented agreement granting it access to a fifth of Venezuela’s oil reserves. By February, Trump’s vision of building an economy and foreign policy around abundant fossil fuel resources appeared to be taking root. The US possessed not only more energy than any rival, but also the ability to use that abundance to shape trade, diplomacy and security. Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran in late February put that doctrine to the test. THE IRAN QUAGMIRE The president initially claimed that the joint campaign with Israel against Iran would last only a few weeks. He also repeatedly indicated that vast US oil and gas resources, together with newfound access to Venezuela’s oil wealth, would shield the economy from any resulting spike in energy costs, which he also suggested would be brief. Those assumptions have not aged well. The war launched on February 28 led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global energy supplies used to flow, triggering one of the largest energy disruptions in modern history. Middle Eastern producers cut output and rerouted exports where possible, while major importers across Asia reduced consumption. This caused oil prices to nearly double in the first two months of the conflict, with global benchmark Brent crude peaking at $118 a barrel in March. That was well below the record [USN:L03220220 TEXT:"$145 reached in 2008"], when Iran-related geopolitical tensions, surging Chinese demand and a weakening US dollar drove prices higher. It was also far less than many had feared, largely thanks to reduced Chinese oil imports, ample crude stocks and the surprising adaptability of global markets. But it still represented a severe shock. Moreover, the risk premium from the Iran war is becoming entrenched. Even though crude flows from the Middle East have mostly recovered, Brent is trading around $110. The conflict has also spread across the Middle East, pulling in most of Washington's Gulf allies, most notably the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, which have suffered multiple deadly attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis. This has upended the market’s confidence in the security of Middle Eastern crude, unravelled longstanding supply routes and sent [USN:L6N45R160 TEXT:"shipping prices"] skyrocketing. Trump wanted to put his stamp on global energy markets, but this was clearly not what he had in mind. PAIN AT THE PUMP In one respect, the 2026 energy shock has vindicated Trump’s strategy. The war cemented the US position as the world’s top supplier of crude, refined fuels and LNG, delivering enormous profits to domestic producers and exporters and allowing the US to expand its position in the global market. Energy independence certainly offered US consumers some protection against the energy shock, particularly compared with Asian economies, where prices and demand destruction were much more extreme this year. But that protection has been far from ironclad. US gasoline prices at the pump climbed above $4.60 a gallon in May, the highest level since 2022, while [USN:L1N45211Q TEXT:"diesel"] surged to a record $6.50 a gallon in September as global refining capacity was squeezed. Those increases rapidly became a political problem for the White House as cost-of-living concerns moved to the forefront of the campaign ahead of the midterms on November 3. The administration sought to contain the fuel-price spike by pulling almost every available lever, including [USN:L6N44M0V8 TEXT:"easing biofuel blending mandates"] and, most controversially, reaching a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"diesel supply agreement"] with Russian President Vladimir Putin. This dynamic underscores the difference between commanding supply and controlling prices. Oil, LNG and refined fuels are internationally traded commodities. US producers sell them at prices shaped by global supply and demand. They don’t typically reserve cheap energy for American households. While Trump briefly floated the idea of a [USN:L6N45E0T3 TEXT:"diesel export ban"], officials ultimately rejected it. Even though a ban might have brought down domestic prices initially, it would likely have resulted in higher fuel prices over the medium term due to global market dynamics. ‘ENERGY SECURITY IS NATIONAL SECURITY’ The administration’s assertion last October that “energy security is national security” appears more relevant than ever. The Iran war has shown that cheap and reliable energy is essential for economic growth, whether it powers heavy industry or the data centres underpinning the artificial intelligence race. But the conflict has also changed the meaning of energy security. For countries dependent on imports, particularly [USN:L6N3ZY18D TEXT:"many in Asia"], the shock has revealed the risks of relying heavily on distant suppliers, vulnerable shipping routes and a concentrated global refining system. Their response is likely to be broader diversification: securing more suppliers, expanding domestic fossil fuel production where possible, accelerating renewable power and shifting more transport towards electricity. That will not kick the US off its lofty energy perch, but it will likely weaken the allure of oil and gas for many countries over the coming years. Trump likely felt emboldened to embark on the Iran war — something his predecessors had baulked at — precisely because US energy independence made a Middle East adventure seem less risky than it had when the US was heavily reliant on Gulf oil and gas. But the conflict has, perhaps permanently, undermined Trump’s promise that energy dominance would guarantee low prices and economic security at home. Hubris can be a dangerous thing. (The opinions expressed here are those of Ron Bousso , a columnist for Reuters.) Enjoying this column? item.title: ＧＭＯ、政府に能動的サイバー防御要請 金銭の要求には応じず
item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 ２４日 ロイター] - ＧＭＯインターネットは２４日、自社のＦＸ（外国為替証拠...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＧＭＯ、政府に能動的サイバー防御要請　金銭の要求には応じず 10/24 14:56 配信

６月５日、千葉県で開催された展示会で撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Issei Kato）

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２４日 ロイター] - ＧＭＯインターネットは２４日、自社のＦＸ（外国為替証拠金取引）の自動売買サービスが受けたサイバー攻撃について、「能動的サイバー防御」の適用を政府に緊急要請したと発表した。攻撃者とみられる相手から同社に対し金銭の要求があり、応じなければ自社や顧客の情報を公開するとの連絡を受けたという。

要求には応じない方針。警察などと連携して対応するとしている。また、サービスの全利用者に一律５０００円の見舞金を支払うことを決めた。

能動的サイバー防御は、被害が深刻化する前に国や関係機関が主導して攻撃者のインフラや侵入経路を特定し、無力化して被害の未然防止を図る仕組み。同社は今回の事案について、一般国民の取引口座（金融資産）を標的とした不正操作・資産毀損という「極めて悪質かつ前例のない手口」だと判断。政府に先制的な対応を求めることを決めた。

同社によると、今月１９日に顧客からの問い合わせを受け調査を開始。２０日にサービスの一部顧客のサーバー環境への不正なプログラムの設置を確認し、２１日には被害拡大防止のため全プランのサーバーを順次停止した。顧客から取引口座での身に覚えのない操作などの報告があり、２２日に警察へ相談したという。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：金価格が回復傾向、中銀・機関投資家需要が支援 焦点：金価格高騰で溶かされる高級時計、希少なビンテージ品喪失に懸念 アングル：本物はドルか金か、中東混乱で「安全資産」巡る議論再燃 コラム：銀は金より高リターン、産業用需要拡大と供給制約が強気材料に コラム：史上最高値から反落の金、今後も強気材料が相場下支えか 最終更新: 10/24(土) 14:56 ロイター

item.title: 米司法省、アラスカ上院選の結果認定阻止へ訴訟 「候補者名酷似」理由に
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米司法省は２２日、１１月中間選挙のアラスカ州連邦上院選で共和党の現職候補が僅差で敗北した場合に、州による選挙結果の認定を差し止めるよう求める訴訟を起こした。投票用紙にほぼ同姓同名の共和党候補が２人記載されており、有権者の混乱を招く恐れがあると主張している。

アラスカは共和党が上院多数派を維持できるかを左右する可能性のある州の一つで、共和党の現職ダン・Ｓ・サリバン氏が、民主党のメアリー・ペルトラ氏と接戦を繰り広げている。

司法省は、選挙にダン・Ｊ・サリバン・ジュニアという名の共和党候補が出馬していることを問題視。訴状は、同氏が「サリバン上院議員の支持者を誤って自身に投票させる意図を持って」立候補していると主張している。

司法省は訴状で、「有権者の混乱の影響を受けた可能性がある」結果の認定を差し止めるよう要請。これにより「ダニエル・Ｊ・サリバン氏に投じられた票が本来はサリバン上院議員に投じられるはずだったものかどうかを調べる調査」が可能になるとしている。

トランプ大統領は２３日、記者団に対して、訴訟を支持すると述べ「やれと言ったのは私だ」と語った。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ＷＳ開幕、ブルワーズが先勝 ミジオロウスキーが最速記録
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は２３日、ワールドシリーズ（ＷＳ、７回戦制）の第１戦を行い、ブルワーズがレイズを３─２で下し、先勝した。

１９８２年以来４４年ぶりのＷＳ出場となったブルワーズは一回、指名打者クリスチャン・イエリチの適時三塁打で先制し、ウィリアム・コントレラス捕手の適時打で２点目を挙げた。

四回に１点を返されたが、七回にはジャクソン・チョウリオ外野手の適時打で１点を追加。九回には１点差に迫られ、２死二、三塁のピンチを迎えたものの、４番手トレバー・メギル投手が最後の打者を三振に仕留めた。

先発ジェーコブ・ミジオロウスキー投手は５回を投げ、４安打１失点、１四球、３三振で勝利投手となった。試合の初球に時速１０３．５マイル（約１６６．６キロ）を計測し、球速の計測が始まった２００８年以降のＷＳ最速記録を樹立した。

item.title: 北朝鮮の金総書記、「軍事革命」加速を要求 精鋭部隊育成へ
item.description: ［ソウル ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ソウル　２４日　ロイター］ - 北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記は、平壌で２日間にわたり開かれた朝鮮人民軍の中隊長会議で、各中隊を自立して戦闘を遂行できる精鋭部隊にするよう求めた。朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）が２４日に伝えた。

今回の会議は、軍事力強化を一貫して政策の優先課題とする金氏の姿勢を鮮明にした。

金氏は１０月２２─２３日に開かれた会議で演説し、「新時代の軍備増強の目標」の達成に向け、全ての中隊が万全の準備を整えるよう求めた。ＫＣＮＡによると、２月の第９回朝鮮労働党大会以降、全軍規模の会議が開かれたのは初めて。

金氏は「最強の軍隊を建設し、われわれの方式による軍事革命を加速させよう」と述べた。

今後５年間の国家の方向性を定める２月の第９回党大会で、金氏は通常戦力の強化を求めるとともに、核兵器とミサイルの開発を進める方針を改めて示していた。

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝八村、古巣レーカーズ戦で16得点 クリッパーズは初黒星
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は２３日、各地で試合を行い、八村塁が先発したクリッパーズはレーカーズに１１７─１２５で敗れ、今季初黒星を喫した。

古巣対戦となった八村は計３３分１６秒の出場で、３本の３点シュートを沈めるなど１６得点、６リバウンド、１アシスト、２スチールだった。ダリアス・ガーランドがチーム最多の２６得点を記録した。レーカーズはオースティン・リーブスが２８得点、９アシストで牽引。ルカ・ドンチッチは２３得点、６リバウンド、７アシストも、１１回のターンオーバーを喫した。

セルティックスは昨季王者のニックスに１０７─１０３で競り勝ち、今季初勝利を挙げた。ジェイソン・テイタムが両チーム最多の３６得点に、９リバウンド、７アシストと活躍。ニックスはカールアンソニー・タウンズ、ＯＧ・アヌノビー、マイルズ・マクブライドの３選手が２０得点以上を記録したが及ばなかった。

ロケッツは昨季西地区覇者のスパーズを１１４─１１０で下した。アルペレン・シェングンが両チーム最多の２９得点に、ケビン・デュラントとアメン・トンプソンも２０得点を記録した。スパーズはビクター・ウェンバンヤマが２５得点、１３リバウンドと奮闘した。

ピストンズはヒートに１２８─１１１で勝利し、２連勝とした。ポール・リードが１９得点、１１リバウンド、３アシストのダブルダブルで貢献。ヒートはヤニス・アデトクンボが３６得点、１２リバウンド、５アシストと躍動したが、チーム全体の３点シュート成功率が２９．４％にとどまり、２連敗となった。

ティンバーウルブズはマジックを１１５─９３で下し、２連勝。そのほか、ホークス、ラプターズ、グリズリーズ、トレイルブレイザーズも２連勝とした。

item.title: ソフトバンクＧ出資のオーペイ、米ＩＰＯで最大44億ドルの評価額目指す
item.description: ［２３日 ロイター］ - ソフトバンクグループが出資するデジタル決済企業オーペイは２３日、米国での新規株式公開（Ｉ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ソフトバンクＧ出資のオーペイ、米ＩＰＯで最大44億ドルの評価額目指す 10/24 13:43 配信

［２３日　ロイター］　 - ソフトバンクグループが出資するデジタル決済企業オーペイは２３日、米国での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）で最大４４億２０００万ドルの評価額を目指すと発表した。新興国で拡大するデジタル金融サービスの需要を取り込む狙い。

ナイジェリアを主力市場とするオーペイは、米国預託株式（ＡＤＳ）約１６００万株を１株当たり１９─２１ドルで売り出し、最大３億６６００万ドルの調達を目指す。

米ＩＰＯ市場は、インフレ率の上昇と人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の急落で圧力にさらされている。新規上場に対する投資家の意欲が後退し、複数の企業が上場計画の延期を余儀なくされる中でのＩＰＯとなる。

オーペイは２０１８年設立。決済、送金、貯蓄、融資などのデジタル金融サービスを提供し、インドネシア、エジプト、パキスタンでも事業を展開している。

世界で６番目に人口が多いナイジェリアは、アフリカ有数のフィンテック市場に成長。調査会社トラクションによると、モニーポイント、フラッターウェーブ、インタースイッチなどのフィンテック企業を輩出している。

提出書類によると、ソフトバンク系企業は今回の売り出し前の時点でオーペイ株の６．６％を保有している。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：静かに進むガソリン離れ、中国製ＥＶの世界展開が後押しか コラム：オープンＡＩ投資で膨らむソフトバンクの財務リスク コラム：孫氏、オープンＡＩへ300億ドル追加投資か　際立つ「一点張り」 最終更新: 10/24(土) 13:43 ロイター

item.title: Saudi Arabia Expands Missile Factory Using Suspected Chinese Technology
item.description: Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two U.S. researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images. More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two U.S. researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images.

More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia to deter attacks by Iran and make its military more self-reliant, while possibly strengthening its position in a deadly conflict with Yemen’s Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.

But they risk fueling a regional missile race and could deepen opposition in the U.S. Congress to a U.S.-Saudi civilian nuclear agreement that has already raised concerns about proliferation.

Satellite company Planet Labs, based in the U.S., took images of the al-Duwadimi complex about 125 miles (200 km) west of Riyadh between April 2025 and September 2026.

The two researchers, Sam Lair and Michael Duitsman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute, assessed that those images show a new building that houses casting pits — wells in which a mixture of fuel ingredients is poured into missile motor casings and allowed to harden.

The Saudi embassy and Information Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

The building, flanked by what appear to be walls to protect nearby structures from accidental explosions, is at least twice as large as the one believed to house the plant’s existing casting pits, Lair and Duitsman said in their assessment. The Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) is a non-partisan research organization in Philadelphia.

They said a second new building could store fuel ingredients or finished missile components.

The imagery “suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges,” they wrote.

Militaries favor solid-fuel missiles because they can be stored for long periods and launched more quickly than liquid-fuel systems.

Lair and Duitsman and experts from the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) and the CNA research and analysis organization told Reuters that the makeup of Saudi Arabia’s missile force suggests that the al-Duwadimi complex relies on Chinese technology. Lair and Duitsman said that its characteristics also are similar to Chinese missile plants.

Saudi Arabia secretly acquired about 40 liquid-fuel DF-3 ballistic missiles from China in 1987, according to a 1991 declassified CIA estimate. It displayed two of them for the first time in an April 2014 military parade, according to a YouTube video and photographs of the event.

The FPRI team also recently identified from social media videos and photos what they assessed was the wreckage in Yemen of a Saudi-fired Chinese-designed DF-15 missile.

Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile.

Riyadh is believed to have turned to Beijing because Washington has long restricted exports of longer-range missile systems.

The Chinese embassy and defense ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The CIA declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

Missiles Would Alter the Balance of Power

Sascha Bruchmann, a research fellow at IISS, said longer-range missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to strike Iran without risking its U.S.-supplied F-15 jet fighters against Iranian air defenses.

“You’d want a system to threaten whatever is holy to Tehran … if you don’t have the political will to send an F-15 with JDAMs over Tehran,” said Bruchmann, referring to U.S.-made satellite-guided bombs. “Iran has a lead because its missiles and drones can strike Saudi wherever it wants. The Saudis could close that capability gap a bit.”

Bruchmann, who reviewed the FPRI analysis at Reuters request, concurred that the expansion of al-Duwadimi could be for producing more powerful solid-fuel missiles.

Janes, the defense intelligence company, also reviewed it and said the buildings “may suggest an effort to expand production capability or support the development of longer-range missiles.”

Saudi Arabia’s apparent pursuit of more powerful missiles comes as other Gulf powers are also seeking to expand their offensive and defensive arsenals, said Decker Eveleth, a CNA analyst who has been tracking the al-Duwadimi construction with commercial satellite imagery and concurred with the FPRI assessment.

“This is being replicated across the Middle East,” he said. “You see exactly the same thing happening in the UAE. You see the exact same thing happening in Turkey. Everybody is doing this now.”

The expansion of al-Duwadimi could have political consequences in the U.S. by stiffening bipartisan congressional opposition to a U.S.-Saudi agreement under which the U.S. would help Riyadh establish uranium enrichment for power generation.

Opponents say that the deal lacks sufficient safeguards to prevent Riyadh from secretly building a nuclear weapon. The kingdom has denied any such plan.

Work Began Last Year

The FPRI assessment said the Planet Labs imagery showed that the expansion at al-Duwadimi began in April 2025 with ground-clearing and digging for the suspected storage building. Work on the suspected casting-pit building began later that month or in early May, it said.

A December 12, 2025, photo showed what researchers assessed were two deep pits inside the building that had no roof yet.

A September 18, 2026, photo shows the roof still partly missing and “heavy-duty blast-diverting walls” on either side to prevent accidental explosions from damaging adjacent structures.

The walls, the researchers said, are somewhat similar to those depicted in imagery of U.S. and Iranian missile plants and “further evidence the building is for casting solid propellant motors.”

Finishing the roofs would not take long, the FPRI said, but installing casting equipment may take several months. The facility could be ready to start producing missiles as early as the end of the year.

item.title: Fire devastates former Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest'
item.description: Firefighters battled for hours to contain a blaze that engulfed the former Nazi guest house known as "The Eagle's Nest" in southern Germany, while police investigated the cause after detaining a man near the scene, authorities said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Firefighters battled for hours to contain a blaze that engulfed the former Nazi guest house known as "The Eagle's Nest" in southern Germany, while police investigated the cause after detaining a man near the scene, authorities said on Saturday. Around 200 firefighters and emergency workers near Berchtesgaden in Bavaria were battling the flames after the building, known as the Kehlsteinhaus, caught fire on Friday, police said. Built in 1938 as a guest house for Nazi officials and their guests, the building sits in a spectacular Alpine setting above Berchtesgaden. Adolf Hitler used it occasionally, earning it the nickname "Hitler's Tea House". It is separate from his nearby summer residence, the Berghof. Bild newspaper quoted a police spokesperson as saying the building, preserved after World War Two as a historical monument linked to the Nazi era, had been so badly damaged that it "could probably not be saved". Police said earlier they had detained a man near the site but had not yet established the cause of the fire. "Whether the person is linked to the fire is currently the subject of a criminal investigation," Bavarian police said in a statement.

item.title: US accuses government contractor of leaking classified info to girlfriend's Substack
item.description: The US Justice Department accused a government contractor on Friday of leaking national defense information to his girlfriend, the publisher of a Substack newsletter.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Trotta
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department accused a government contractor on Friday of leaking national defense information to his girlfriend, the publisher of a Substack newsletter. The FBI arrested Ian Brinksman, 42, on Friday following a search of his Washington home, a Justice Department statement said. Prosecutors charged him with unlawfully transmitting national defense information. A federal public defender representing Brinksman declined to comment. “As alleged, Brinksman reached far outside his own duties to obtain some of our Nation’s most closely held secrets and handed them to a romantic partner he knew intended to publish them,” John Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for national security, said in the statement. “That is not carelessness. It is a betrayal of his oath and the American people who entrusted him to fulfill his duties honorably,” Eisenberg said. Brinksman held a top secret security clearance while working as an employee of a US government agency and later as a developer for systems integration for a private contractor working for the same agency, prosecutors said. According to the sworn affidavit of an FBI agent investigating the case, Brinksman repeatedly accessed classified intelligence reports and then communicated with the journalist. The affidavit also cites phone records, database access logs, badge-swipe records, emails and other evidence. The affidavit only identifies the journalist as "Individual 1," but it cites excerpts from articles she published. "A fundraising article reportedly published by Individual 1 in September 2026 stated 'over the past year (Individual 1 has) published reporting based on classified (relevant U.S. government agency) assessments that I believe the public deserves to know about,'" the affidavit reads. That quote appears in a September 28 piece published on the Capital & Empire online newsletter authored by Aída Chávez. "Over the past year, I’ve published reporting based on classified CIA assessments that I believe the public deserves to know about," wrote Chávez, whose profile on the site notes that she worked for the Nation and other outlets before she launched the newsletter. Chávez did not respond to an email message seeking comment. Investigators allege that on at least five occasions in 2026, Individual 1 published Substack articles containing information that mirrored the classified reports, some at the top secret level. On some of those dates, Chávez published articles that cite classified reports, some of them attributed to the CIA. According to a LinkedIn profile bearing Brinksman's name, he worked for Deloitte as a manager and as a senior strategy security consultant after having worked as a US State Department foreign service officer on dates corresponding to those outlined in the Justice Department statement. The State Department declined to comment. Deloitte did not respond to requests for comment.

item.title: Ｆ１＝ハミルトンが現役続行の可能性示唆、アフリカでのレース開催計画受け
item.description: ［オースティン（米テキサス州） ２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［オースティン（米テキサス州）　２２日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１で個人総合優勝７回を誇るルイス・ハミルトン（英国、フェラーリ）は２２日、ルワンダでのグランプリ（ＧＰ）開催が現役生活を長く続けていく原動力になり得ると語った。

Ｆ１は１３日、２０３０年代初頭から１０年間にわたりルワンダでＧＰを開催することで合意したことを発表した。

今季の総合首位につけるキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）と共に今週末の米国ＧＰに向けた記者会見に出席したハミルトンは、アフリカＧＰの復活について、「アフリカでのレース開催が決まったことで、より長く現役を続けなければならなくなった。アフリカでレースをすることは、ずっと私の夢だった」と述べた。

来年１月に４２歳となるハミルトンは続けて、「コンディションを維持するために戦い続けなければならない。来年も良い結果を残し続けることができれば、このまま現役を続けていくつもりだ」とコメント。２０歳のアントネッリは「少なくとも最初のレースには出ないと」とハミルトンを鼓舞した。

Ｆ１史上初で唯一の黒人の王者であるハミルトンは、アフリカでのレース開催を長年にわたり訴え続けてきた。これまでの自身の取り組みについても語り、「私にとってアフリカはＧＰ開催にふさわしい場所だ。単に一つの国だけの問題ではなく、アフリカ大陸そのものにとって重要なことだ」と述べた。

Pentagon designates China-funded Confucius Institutes as US national security threat

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth accused China-funded Confucius Institutes of stealing intellectual property and spreading propaganda on American university campuses.

WASHINGTON: The US Defense Department has designated Chinese-funded cultural centers on university campuses known as Confucius Institutes as a threat to the United States' national security, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Friday (Oct 23). Washington has long accused Confucius Institutes of being Chinese propaganda tools and has taken steps to crack down on them. Hegseth, in a video posted on social media, alleged that Confucius Institutes were operating under disguise at US universities and that the Pentagon had added them to its list of institutions that threaten US national security. "It turns out that 80 new propaganda cells across 30 universities had popped up using different names and different charters, but with the same mission: to steal intellectual property and to infiltrate the minds of American students," Hegseth said.

item.title: ＥＵ、貿易赤字削減へ中国との対話重視 化学品や機械などの輸入抑制模索
item.description: ［ダブリン ２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ダブリン　２３日　ロイター］ - 欧州連合（ＥＵ）の閣僚らは２３日、域内経済に打撃を与えている対中貿易赤字の削減に向けて化学品や機械などの製品の輸入を抑制することを目指し、中国政府との対話に注力すべきとの認識で一致した。

シェフチョビッチ欧州委員（通商担当）は今月、中国からのハイブリッド車の輸入を半分超削減することで中国政府と合意した。１日当たり１０億ユーロ（１１億２０００万ドル）超に膨らんだ対中貿易赤字に対処するとともに、苦境にある欧州自動車メーカーを支援する。

アイルランドのマッケンティー外相はダブリンでの閣僚会合後の会見で、欧州委員会が中国との対話を継続すべきだという点で、ＥＵ加盟国全てが一致していると説明。「ハイブリッド車以外に、化学品や機械など他の分野に目を向けたいという非常に明確な意向がある」と語った。その上で、対話が優先事項である一方、不均衡を解消するために既存の貿易防衛手段を活用することも可能だと指摘した。

シェフチョビッチ氏は、プラスチックのセーフガード（緊急輸入制限）に関する調査が次に開始される見通しだと述べた。「調査開始に必要な要件が全てそろっているかどうかを検討している」とした。

item.title: Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say
item.description: Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington collapses.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say

Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington collapses.

Vessels at the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, Oct 23, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Stringer)

FAST

DUBAI: Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters. Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington collapses. The two Iranian security officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, gave few details and did not say how or where exactly Tehran would carry out such attacks. But one of them said Iran would aim to prevent repairs after any attacks to prolong disruptions to communications, including internet connections. "If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines ... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one of the officials said.
